text: For when God made a promise to Abraham, because He could swear by no one greater, He swore by Himself, saying, "Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you."
simplify: When God made his promise to Abraham, since no one greater existed to swear by, he swore by himself. This shows the reader how seriously and personally God backs his promises. God promised Abraham that he would surely bless him and greatly multiply his descendants. The reader sees that God's promises are specific, generous, and certain.

text: The LORD is my strength and my shield; My heart trusted in Him, and I am helped; Therefore my heart greatly rejoices, And with my song I will praise Him.
simplify: The Lord is David's strength and shield; he trusted God, was helped, and now his heart overflows with joy and song. It means trusting God in hard times brings real help and deep joy.

text: And my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
simplify: God will supply what you actually need out of his riches. Not everything you want, but what you need.

text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to His abundant mercy has begotten us again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an inheritance incorruptible and undefiled and that does not fade away, reserved in heaven for you, who are kept by the power of God through faith for salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
simplify: God's mercy gave believers a fresh start and a hope that won't die, secured by Jesus rising from the dead. This gives the reader solid reason to praise God. God is keeping an inheritance for believers that is pure, lasting, and untouched by decay. It means the future God promises you is safe and cannot be lost. God's power guards believers through their trust in him until the full salvation he has prepared is revealed. You are being kept safe by God himself, not by your own strength.

text: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.
simplify: God loved the world enough to give his Son, so that trusting him means living forever. Love is the motive; the cross is the cost.

text: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God; and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
simplify: Do not carry it; pray it, with thanks. And God's peace stands guard over your heart.

text: Blessed are the peacemakers, For they shall be called sons of God.
simplify: Those who work to make peace are blessed and will be called God's children. It means peacemaking is a family trait of God's people.

text: Heal me, O LORD, and I shall be healed; Save me, and I shall be saved, For You are my praise.
simplify: Jeremiah asks God to heal and save him, confessing that God is his hope. The reader can bring their need for healing and rescue to God with confidence.

text: No weapon formed against you shall prosper, And every tongue which rises against you in judgment You shall condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, And their righteousness is from Me," Says the LORD.
simplify: God promises that no weapon made against his people will work and every accusing voice will be proven wrong, because their right standing comes from him. The reader can stand secure, defended by God against attacks and false accusations.

text: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
simplify: If you lack wisdom, ask God, who gives freely. He does not shame people for asking.

text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
simplify: Confess and he forgives and cleanses, fully. Confession is not begging; it is a promise being kept.

text: Delight yourself also in the LORD, And He shall give you the desires of your heart.
simplify: Delighting in God changes what you want. He then shapes your desires to match what he is already giving.

text: My brethren, take the prophets, who spoke in the name of the Lord, as an example of suffering and patience.
simplify: Look at the prophets who spoke for the Lord as examples of suffering patiently and enduring trouble. When you suffer, you can look at how faithful people before you endured and follow their example.

text: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, in everything give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
simplify: Rejoice, pray, give thanks: this is God's will, not a suggestion. Gratitude is a way of living, not a mood.

text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any trouble, with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
simplify: Paul praises God, calling him the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort. This tells the reader that God is the source of every kindness and every bit of comfort they will ever need. God comforts us in all our troubles so that we can pass that same comfort on to others who are struggling. Your own hard times can become the very thing that lets you help someone else.

text: Whenever I am afraid, I will trust in You. In God (I will praise His word), In God I have put my trust; I will not fear. What can flesh do to me?
simplify: Fear is allowed to show up; what you do with it matters. When it comes, trust is the answer. Because God has promised to help, David can praise him and stop being afraid of what people might do. What people can do to you matters less than what God has promised.

text: This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate in it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success.
simplify: God tells Joshua to keep the book of the law in his thoughts and speech constantly, so he will obey it carefully. It means filling our minds with God's word leads to doing well in life.

text: Therefore I say to you, whatever things you ask when you pray, believe that you receive them, and you will have them. "And whenever you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive him, that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses.
simplify: Pray expecting that God hears you. Trusting him is part of the praying. When you pray, forgive anyone you have something against, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your sins too. Holding grudges blocks the forgiveness we want from God.

text: Now may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the patience of Christ.
simplify: Paul prays that the Lord directs their hearts into God's love and into patient endurance like Christ's. It means letting God shape your love and your patience.

text: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.
simplify: Anyone in Christ is a new creation, with the old gone. It is not just forgiveness; it is a fresh start.

text: No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.
simplify: Every temptation comes with a way out, because God is faithful. You are not trapped; look for the exit.

text: "Most assuredly, I say to you, he who believes in Me, the works that I do he will do also; and greater works than these he will do, because I go to My Father.
simplify: Jesus says those who trust him will do the same works he did, and even greater ones, because he is going to the Father. Your faith connects you to a power bigger than yourself, not a smaller imitation.

text: Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ.
simplify: Paul tells the Corinthians to copy his way of living because he copies Christ. For you, it means looking at how faithful believers live as a pattern for following Jesus.

text: Then Jesus said to him, "Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will by no means believe."
simplify: Jesus pointed out that people tend to want signs and miracles before they will believe. It warns us that faith based only on spectacular evidence can be shallow.

text: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
simplify: Sin pays death; God gives life through Jesus. Two wages, one choice.

text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says the LORD, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope. Then you will call upon Me and go and pray to Me, and I will listen to you. And you will seek Me and find Me, when you search for Me with all your heart.
simplify: God's plan for his people is good, even while they wait in a hard season. A plan can be real before it is visible. God says they will call on him and pray, and he will listen. Prayer is not wasted; God pays attention to people who cry out to him. If they look for God with their whole heart, they will find him. God is found by those who seek him sincerely, not half-heartedly.

text: "Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, And whose hope is the LORD. For he shall be like a tree planted by the waters, Which spreads out its roots by the river, And will not fear when heat comes; But its leaf will be green, And will not be anxious in the year of drought, Nor will cease from yielding fruit.
simplify: God blesses the person who trusts in Him and puts their hope in Him. The reader is encouraged that trusting God brings real blessing. That person is like a tree planted by water with roots reaching the stream—it doesn't fear heat, stays green, and keeps bearing fruit even in drought. It means trusting God gives steady strength in hard times.

text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.
simplify: Every good and perfect gift comes from above, from the Father of lights, who never changes. The reader can trust that God's goodness is constant.

text: To them God willed to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
simplify: That revealed secret is Christ living in them, including non-Jewish believers, which is the sure hope of future glory. It means God's presence inside a person is the guarantee of what is to come.

text: But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
simplify: God loved us before we were worth loving. Grace is not a reward for good behaviour.

text: He gives power to the weak, And to those who have no might He increases strength. Even the youths shall faint and be weary, And the young men shall utterly fall, But those who wait on the LORD Shall renew their strength; They shall mount up with wings like eagles, They shall run and not be weary, They shall walk and not faint.
simplify: God gives strength to the tired and power to those who have none. For the reader, it means when you're exhausted, God is the one who can renew you. Even young people get tired and worn out and stumble. For the reader, it means human strength has limits, so don't be ashamed when you reach yours. Waiting on God is not doing nothing; it is drawing strength from him. That strength outlasts your own.

text: I will both lie down in peace, and sleep; For You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
simplify: You can lie down and actually sleep, because God is the one keeping watch. Rest is trust in action.

text: He heals the brokenhearted And binds up their wounds.
simplify: God heals people whose hearts are crushed and tenderly cares for their wounds. It means your deepest hurts matter to him and he is at work mending them.

text: But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
simplify: The Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from evil. You can trust God to hold you steady when things are hard.

text: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, And lean not on your own understanding; In all your ways acknowledge Him, And He shall direct your paths.
simplify: Trust means leaning on God instead of your own read of things. He straightens the road as you go.

text: And forgive us our debts, As we forgive our debtors.
simplify: Ask God to forgive your debts, just as you forgive those who owe you. Receiving God's forgiveness goes together with forgiving others.

text: You will show me the path of life; In Your presence is fullness of joy; At Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
simplify: God shows David the path of life, and being with God brings full joy and lasting pleasure. It tells the reader that the deepest and most enduring happiness is found in God's presence.

text: Do not fear any of those things which you are about to suffer. Indeed, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and you will have tribulation ten days. Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
simplify: Jesus tells them not to fear coming suffering, including prison and testing, and to stay faithful even to death. It means hard times are real, but faithfulness is rewarded with life.

text: Enter into His gates with thanksgiving, And into His courts with praise. Be thankful to Him, and bless His name.
simplify: Thanksgiving is the doorway into God's presence. And his goodness is not a mood that changes.

text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil; For You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
simplify: The Lord leads, provides and protects all the way through. Even in the darkest valley, you are not walking alone.

text: For you did not receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption by whom we cry out, "Abba, Father."
simplify: You didn't receive a spirit of fear and slavery again, but a spirit of adoption as sons and daughters, by which we cry out to God as Father. You can approach God with confidence as his child, not with fear.

text: Let them shout for joy and be glad, Who favor my righteous cause; And let them say continually, "Let the LORD be magnified, Who has pleasure in the prosperity of His servant."
simplify: He asks that those who support him shout for joy and praise God, who is pleased when his servant has peace. It means God cares about your well-being, and your friends should rejoice when you are helped.

text: Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The effective, fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much. Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain; and it did not rain on the land for three years and six months. And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.
simplify: Confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so you can be healed; the prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective. Being honest about your sins and praying for one another brings real help and healing. Elijah was a human being just like us, yet he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it didn't rain for three and a half years. Ordinary people who pray can see God do extraordinary things. Then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain and the earth produced its fruit. Persistent prayer matters, and God answers it in his time.

text: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants--things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John, who bore witness to the word of God, and to the testimony of Jesus Christ, to all things that he saw.
simplify: God gave Jesus this message so his followers could know what is going to happen soon, and Jesus passed it on through an angel to John. It means the book comes from God and is meant to prepare you for what's ahead. John faithfully reported everything he saw and heard about God's message and Jesus. It means the writer is telling you this account is trustworthy and based on what he actually witnessed.

text: Behold, I will do a new thing, Now it shall spring forth; Shall you not know it? I will even make a road in the wilderness And rivers in the desert.
simplify: God says he is doing something new that is already beginning, and he will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. Watch for God's new work, even in barren places.

text: Therefore submit to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you.
simplify: Submit yourself to God and stand against the devil, and he will flee from you. Put yourself under God's authority and resist evil with his strength.

text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
simplify: God made everything, and he made it on purpose. Nothing exists by accident, including you.

text: "Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land which the LORD your God is giving you.
simplify: Honouring your parents comes with a promise attached. God ties blessing to the way you treat the people who raised you.

text: And they went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs. Amen.
simplify: The disciples went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked with them, confirming the message with signs. When we share the good news, Jesus himself works alongside us to make it effective.

text: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast.
simplify: Saved by grace through faith, not by works. So nobody has anything to boast about.

text: Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.
simplify: Baptism pictured being buried with Christ, and just as the Father raised him, we are meant to live a new kind of life. It means your life should show the fresh start God has given you.

text: Trust in the LORD, and do good; Dwell in the land, and feed on His faithfulness.
simplify: Trust God and keep doing what's right, and settle down where you are. Your job is to live faithfully, not to fret about others.

text: For I, the LORD your God, will hold your right hand, Saying to you, "Fear not, I will help you.'
simplify: God says he holds his people's hand and tells them not to be afraid because he will help. It means we are not alone; God himself is with us and supports us.

text: Now hope does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
simplify: That hope won't leave us disappointed, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit he gave us. For you, this means you can trust your hope because God's love is real inside you.

text: The LORD your God in your midst, The Mighty One, will save; He will rejoice over you with gladness, He will quiet you with His love, He will rejoice over you with singing."
simplify: God is not disappointed to be near you; he rejoices over you quietly. He is glad you are his.

text: Concerning this thing I pleaded with the Lord three times that it might depart from me. And He said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness." Therefore most gladly I will rather boast in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in needs, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ's sake. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
simplify: Paul asked the Lord three times to take this thorn away. For the reader, this is an example of honest, persistent prayer when we are hurting. God's grace is enough even when you are not. His strength shows up best where you are weakest. Paul says he takes pleasure in weaknesses, insults, hardships, attacks, and troubles for Christ's sake, because when he is weak, then he is strong. This tells the reader that God's strength shows up best in our weakness.

text: If it is possible, as much as depends on you, live peaceably with all men.
simplify: Do everything you can on your side to live at peace with everyone.

text: For I will restore health to you And heal you of your wounds,' says the LORD, "Because they called you an outcast saying: "This is Zion; No one seeks her."' "Thus says the LORD: "Behold, I will bring back the captivity of Jacob's tents, And have mercy on his dwelling places; The city shall be built upon its own mound, And the palace shall remain according to its own plan.
simplify: God promises to heal his people and mend their wounds. He does this partly because others had written them off as abandoned and worthless. God promises to restore the homes and towns of his people and show them mercy. Ruined places will be rebuilt and lived in again.

text: You whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, And called from its farthest regions, And said to you, "You are My servant, I have chosen you and have not cast you away: Fear not, for I am with you; Be not dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, Yes, I will help you, I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.'
simplify: God says he called his people from far away and chose them, and he has not rejected them. It means God's commitment to his people does not depend on distance or circumstance. Do not panic: God is with you, will strengthen you, and will hold you up. Four promises in one sentence.

text: You are my hiding place; You shall preserve me from trouble; You shall surround me with songs of deliverance.Selah I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will guide you with My eye.
simplify: God is a hiding place that keeps you safe from trouble and surrounds you with songs of rescue. You can trust him to protect you when things are hard. God promises to teach you and show you the right way to go, watching over you as you walk. You are not left to figure life out alone; he will guide you.

text: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, put on tender mercies, kindness, humility, meekness, longsuffering; bearing with one another, and forgiving one another, if anyone has a complaint against another; even as Christ forgave you, so you also must do.
simplify: As God's chosen, holy, and dearly loved people, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. These qualities should shape how you treat people. Bear with each other and forgive whatever grievances you have, just as the Lord forgave you. Since you've been forgiven, extend that same forgiveness.

text: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
simplify: Hope, joy and peace come from God, not from good circumstances. Hope is meant to overflow.

text: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for He who promised is faithful.
simplify: Let's hold tightly to our hope without wavering, because the one who made the promise is faithful. Your hope rests on God's reliability, not your feelings.

text: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.
simplify: Let Christ's peace rule in your hearts, since you were called into one body, and be thankful. Let peace, not conflict, guide your decisions and relationships.

text: Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For My yoke is easy and My burden is light."
simplify: Jesus invites the tired to come, not to try harder. Rest is something he gives. Jesus invited people to take his yoke on themselves and learn from him, because he is gentle and humble, and promised rest for their souls. A yoke is a burden harness, so he's saying life with him is a shared load, and the weary reader is offered real rest rather than more pressure. Jesus said his yoke is good and the weight he gives is not hard. Following him still involves work, but it's a kind, bearable load rather than a crushing one, and the reader can trust that Jesus won't overload them.

text: Though an army may encamp against me, My heart shall not fear; Though war may rise against me, In this I will be confident.
simplify: Even if a whole army surrounds him, David says his heart stays calm and his trust holds firm. For the reader, it means courage does not come from having no danger but from trusting God in the middle of it.

text: The Elder, To the beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth: Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be in health, just as your soul prospers.
simplify: The writer, a church leader, is writing to a dear friend named Gaius, whom he genuinely loves. It shows that faith creates real, warm friendships worth naming and honoring. He prays that Gaius will do well and stay healthy, just as his spiritual life is already strong. It's a reminder that caring for someone's whole well-being, body and soul, is a good and loving prayer.

text: You lust and do not have. You murder and covet and cannot obtain. You fight and war. Yet you do not have because you do not ask. You ask and do not receive, because you ask amiss, that you may spend it on your pleasures.
simplify: People want things badly, don't get them, and end up in envy, fighting, and even violence. The real reason you don't have what you want is that you never ask God for it. Even when you do ask, you don't receive because your motives are wrong—you only want things to satisfy your own pleasure. Check whether what you're praying for is really about you or about God.

text: This is a faithful saying: For if we died with Him, We shall also live with Him. If we endure, We shall also reign with Him. If we deny Him, He also will deny us. If we are faithless, He remains faithful; He cannot deny Himself.
simplify: This saying is trustworthy: if we died with him, we will also live with him. For the reader, it means sharing in Christ's death means sharing in his life. If we endure, we will reign with him; if we disown him, he will disown us. For the reader, it means perseverance matters, and denying Christ has real consequences. Even when we are faithless, he remains faithful, because he cannot deny who he is. For the reader, it means God's faithfulness does not depend on yours, which is both comfort and a call to trust him.

text: Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed, Because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; Great is Your faithfulness. "The LORD is my portion," says my soul, "Therefore I hope in Him!"
simplify: God's mercy did not run out overnight. Every morning it starts again, and he stays faithful. He tells himself that the Lord is his portion, so he will put his hope in him. It invites the reader to find enough in God himself to keep hoping.

text: Then, when desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, brings forth death.
simplify: Desire, once it takes hold, gives birth to sin, and sin when full-grown leads to death. The reader is warned to stop small wrong desires before they grow.

text: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
simplify: Because of this sure hope, stand firm and keep working for the Lord. Nothing you do for him is wasted, even when you cannot see the results.

text: Train up a child in the way he should go, And when he is old he will not depart from it.
simplify: Start a child in the right direction early. What is planted young tends to stay planted.

text: For I will not dare to speak of any of those things which Christ has not accomplished through me, in word and deed, to make the Gentiles obedient-- in mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God, so that from Jerusalem and round about to Illyricum I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.
simplify: Paul will only speak of what Christ has done through him to bring the Gentiles to obedience, by word and deed. Point to what God has done, not to yourself. Paul spread the good news from Jerusalem all the way to Illyricum, backed by signs and wonders and the Spirit's power. God's power works through ordinary people to spread his message.

text: "Most assuredly, I say to you, he who hears My word and believes in Him who sent Me has everlasting life, and shall not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.
simplify: Anyone who hears Jesus' word and believes in the one who sent him has eternal life and won't be condemned; they have already passed from death to life. Trusting Jesus brings life now, not just later.

text: And whatever things you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive."
simplify: He promised that whatever they ask for in prayer, believing, they will receive. Prayer with genuine trust in God gets results.

text: "Let not your heart be troubled; you believe in God, believe also in Me.
simplify: Jesus tells his worried friends not to let fear take over their hearts, but to trust God and also to trust him. Whatever is making you anxious, you can bring that fear to God and to Jesus instead of carrying it alone.

text: Therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in due time, casting all your care upon Him, for He cares for you.
simplify: Humble yourself and cast your care on him, because he cares for you. Both the bowing and the handing over.

text: For we were saved in this hope, but hope that is seen is not hope; for why does one still hope for what he sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly wait for it with perseverance.
simplify: Our salvation is something we hope for, but hope that is already seen isn't really hope. You are saved in a way that still requires trusting in what you can't yet see. If we hope for what we don't yet see, we wait for it patiently. Trusting God means holding on with patience while you wait for his promises.

text: Behold what manner of love the Father has bestowed on us, that we should be called children of God! Therefore the world does not know us, because it did not know Him.
simplify: God's love is so great that he calls us his own children, and that is truly what we are. It means you can be confident you belong to God's family, even when others don't understand it.

text: You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world.
simplify: You belong to God and have already overcome these false teachers, because God's Spirit in you is stronger than the spirit at work in the world. You need not be afraid of deceptive voices.

text: For to be carnally minded is death, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
simplify: A mind set on selfish desires leads to death, but a mind set on the Spirit brings life and peace. What you focus your thoughts on shapes your whole life.

text: But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities; The chastisement for our peace was upon Him, And by His stripes we are healed.
simplify: The punishment that brought us peace fell on him. Healing comes at his cost, not at ours.

text: Be strong and of good courage, do not fear nor be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, He is the One who goes with you. He will not leave you nor forsake you."
simplify: God goes ahead of you and will not walk out on you. Courage is possible because you are not going alone.

text: For the LORD gives wisdom; From His mouth come knowledge and understanding; He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield to those who walk uprightly; He guards the paths of justice, And preserves the way of His saints.
simplify: Wisdom doesn't come from us; God is the one who gives it, and real knowledge and understanding come from him. It means when you find wisdom, you should thank God for it rather than pat yourself on the back. God has help ready for people who live honestly, and he protects those who mean well. It means doing right isn't wasted; God stands guard over you. God watches over the paths of people who do right and looks after those who respect him. It means you are not walking through life unnoticed or unprotected.

text: And be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God in Christ forgave you.
simplify: Be kind and forgive, because you were forgiven first. The reason comes before the rule.

text: Go, eat your bread with joy, And drink your wine with a merry heart; For God has already accepted your works.
simplify: The writer tells us to eat our food happily and drink with a glad heart, because God is pleased with what we do. Enjoying simple daily gifts is good and right.

text: Take heed to yourself and to the doctrine. Continue in them, for in doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
simplify: Watch your own life and your teaching closely and keep at it, because doing so will bring salvation to you and to those who listen. It means our personal integrity and our message both matter for ourselves and others.

text: And whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
simplify: Whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God through him. Every part of your life can be done as an offering to him.

text: Let, I pray, Your merciful kindness be for my comfort, According to Your word to Your servant.
simplify: He asks God's mercy to comfort him, just as God promised. It means we can look to God's promises for comfort.

text: For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
simplify: Nothing in life or death can separate you from God's love. The list is exhausting, and it is complete.

text: Blessed is the man Who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, Nor stands in the path of sinners, Nor sits in the seat of the scornful; But his delight is in the law of the LORD, And in His law he meditates day and night. He shall be like a tree Planted by the rivers of water, That brings forth its fruit in its season, Whose leaf also shall not wither; And whatever he does shall prosper.
simplify: What you plant yourself in shapes what you become. A life rooted in God's word bears fruit in its season.

text: Likewise the Spirit also helps in our weaknesses. For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
simplify: The Spirit helps us in our weakness, because we don't know how to pray properly, and the Spirit intercedes for us with groans too deep for words. When you don't know what to pray, the Spirit prays for you.

text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away.
simplify: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away. Everything else can fail, but what Jesus says is completely reliable.

text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves torment. But he who fears has not been made perfect in love.
simplify: Perfect love drives out fear, because fear involves punishment and shows love isn't yet complete. The more you rest in God's love, the less you need to be afraid.

text: Let no one say when he is tempted, "I am tempted by God"; for God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He Himself tempt anyone.
simplify: No one should say God is tempting them to do evil, since God cannot be tempted by evil and tempts no one. The reader should not blame God for their own pull toward wrong.

text: And He was handed the book of the prophet Isaiah. And when He had opened the book, He found the place where it was written: "The Spirit of the LORD is upon Me, Because He has anointed Me To preach the gospel to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives And recovery of sight to the blind, To set at liberty those who are oppressed; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD."
simplify: He was handed the scroll of Isaiah and opened it to a particular passage. God's word was central to what Jesus came to do. Jesus read that God's Spirit had chosen him to bring good news to the poor, heal the brokenhearted, free prisoners, give sight to the blind, and release the oppressed. His mission is good news for people who are hurting. The passage announced a time when the Lord shows his favor. Jesus came to bring that season of God's kindness.

text: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well pleasing to the Lord.
simplify: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord. Honoring your parents is part of following Christ.

text: This beginning of signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and manifested His glory; and His disciples believed in Him.
simplify: This was Jesus' first miracle, and it revealed who he really was, leading his disciples to believe in him. Seeing what Jesus does should move us to trust him more.

text: Jesus said to him, "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
simplify: He is the way, the truth and the life. That is a claim to follow, not a theory to debate.

text: I have been young, and now am old; Yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, Nor his descendants begging bread.
simplify: The psalmist, now old, has never seen a righteous person abandoned or their children begging for food. God's care proves reliable over a lifetime.

text: You will keep him in perfect peace, Whose mind is stayed on You, Because he trusts in You.
simplify: God keeps steady, peaceful people whose minds are fixed on him, because they put their hope in him. It means trusting God brings real peace, even when life is hard.

text: John bore witness of Him and cried out, saying, "This was He of whom I said, "He who comes after me is preferred before me, for He was before me."' And of His fullness we have all received, and grace for grace.
simplify: John testified about Jesus, saying that the one coming after him ranks above him because he existed before him. This means Jesus is greater than John, even though John came first in time. From Jesus' fullness we have all received grace upon grace. This means Jesus keeps giving us generous gifts of kindness we don't deserve.

text: And now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.
simplify: Faith, hope, and love remain, and love is the greatest of the three. Of everything you can pursue, love is the most important.

text: And we have known and believed the love that God has for us. God is love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God in him.
simplify: We have come to know and trust the love God has for us, because God is love and those who live in love live in him. Trusting his love changes how you live.

text: If anyone speaks, let him speak as the oracles of God. If anyone ministers, let him do it as with the ability which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
simplify: If you speak, speak as one speaking God's words; if you serve, serve with the strength God supplies, so that in everything God gets the glory through Jesus Christ. Everything you do should point people to God, not to yourself.

text: For God is not the author of confusion but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.
simplify: God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches. Worship should reflect his character by being peaceful and orderly.

text: But may the God of all grace, who called us to His eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
simplify: After a short time of suffering, the God of grace will himself restore, strengthen, and establish you in his eternal glory through Christ. Your pain is temporary, and God promises to make you whole.

text: The angel of the LORD encamps all around those who fear Him, And delivers them.
simplify: God's angel stands guard around those who honour him and keeps them safe. The reader can trust that God watches over those who revere him.

text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, But fools despise wisdom and instruction.
simplify: Respecting the Lord and taking him seriously is where real knowledge begins, but foolish people refuse wisdom and correction. If you want to learn, start by honoring God rather than dismissing what he says.

text: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
simplify: There is now no condemnation for those in Christ. The verdict has already been settled.

text: Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say, rejoice!
simplify: Paul tells them to rejoice in the Lord always, and then says it again for emphasis. It means your joy comes from the Lord, not your circumstances, so you can be glad even now.

text: Now we exhort you, brethren, warn those who are unruly, comfort the fainthearted, uphold the weak, be patient with all.
simplify: Warn those who are out of line, encourage the timid, help the weak, and be patient with everyone. Different people need different kinds of care, and patience is required for all.

text: Offer to God thanksgiving, And pay your vows to the Most High.
simplify: God tells them to offer thanksgiving and to keep their promises to him. It means what God really wants is grateful hearts and kept commitments, not empty rituals.

text: Blessed are those who mourn, For they shall be comforted.
simplify: Those who are grieving or sad are blessed because God will comfort them. It means your sorrow is not the end, and God promises to bring you relief.

text: Are not two sparrows sold for a copper coin? And not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father's will. But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not fear therefore; you are of more value than many sparrows.
simplify: Two sparrows are sold for a tiny coin, yet not one of them dies without your Father knowing. God notices even the smallest, cheapest creatures. Even the hairs on your head are all counted. God knows you in far more detail than you know yourself. So they should not be afraid, because they are worth more than a whole flock of sparrows. If God cares for small birds, he surely cares for people.

text: Through wisdom a house is built, And by understanding it is established; By knowledge the rooms are filled With all precious and pleasant riches.
simplify: A home is built well through wisdom, and it stands firm through good sense. Lasting homes come from thoughtful choices, not luck. Knowledge fills a house with good and pleasant things. Learning and understanding bring real value to everyday life.

text: But you, when you pray, go into your room, and when you have shut your door, pray to your Father who is in the secret place; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
simplify: Pray alone with the door shut, and God, who sees what is secret, will reward you. Honest prayer is directed to God, not performed for people.

text: The LORD is righteous in all His ways, Gracious in all His works.
simplify: God is right in everything he does and kind in all his works. It assures the reader that God's actions are always fair and loving, never cruel or unjust.

text: Though your beginning was small, Yet your latter end would increase abundantly.
simplify: Bildad says that even if Job's beginnings were small, God would make his future great. He is offering hope, but only on the condition that Job is innocent.

text: For we do not have a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses, but was in all points tempted as we are, yet without sin.
simplify: Our high priest isn't distant from our weaknesses; Jesus was tempted in every way we are, yet he never sinned. That means he truly understands what we struggle with.

text: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
simplify: God doesn't take back his gifts or his call. What he has chosen and promised stays firm.

text: Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
simplify: This is why a man leaves his father and mother and joins with his wife, and the two become one. Marriage is meant to be a close, lasting bond that forms a new family.

text: For if the word spoken through angels proved steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just reward, how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation, which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed to us by those who heard Him, God also bearing witness both with signs and wonders, with various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to His own will?
simplify: The message given through angels was firm, and every violation of it received a fair punishment. This shows that God takes his messages seriously. If we ignore such a great salvation, we will not escape; this salvation was first announced by the Lord and then confirmed by those who heard him. The reader should not treat this salvation casually. God backed up their message with signs, wonders, miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit given as he chose. This confirms that the message is truly from God.

text: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.
simplify: John wrote these things so that believers could be sure they have eternal life. You do not have to live in doubt about where you stand with God.

text: Now to Abraham and his Seed were the promises made. He does not say, "And to seeds," as of many, but as of one, "And to your Seed," who is Christ.
simplify: The promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring, and Paul says this points to one person, Christ. It means God's promise was ultimately fulfilled in Jesus.

text: The fear of man brings a snare, But whoever trusts in the LORD shall be safe.
simplify: Fearing what people think is a trap, but trusting the Lord keeps you safe. It encourages the reader to put confidence in God rather than in others' approval.

text: But if you indeed obey His voice and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries.
simplify: If you truly listen to God's voice and do what he says, he will oppose those who oppose you and fight those who fight you. Obedience brings God's protection and help.

text: Do not let your heart envy sinners, But be zealous for the fear of the LORD all the day; For surely there is a hereafter, And your hope will not be cut off.
simplify: Don't envy those who do wrong, but keep honoring the Lord all day long. Reverence for God is better than longing for what sinners have. There is surely a future ahead, and your hope will not be crushed. Living rightly is worth it because hope lies ahead.

text: I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.
simplify: You are no longer living for yourself; Christ lives in you. Faith is trusting the one who gave himself.

text: But the Lord stood with me and strengthened me, so that the message might be preached fully through me, and that all the Gentiles might hear. Also I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
simplify: The Lord stood with Paul and gave him strength so the message could be fully preached to the Gentiles, and Paul was rescued. It means God is faithful to help us when everyone else is gone.

text: Great peace have those who love Your law, And nothing causes them to stumble.
simplify: People who love God's law enjoy deep peace and are kept from stumbling. Loving what God says brings a steadiness that keeps you from falling.

text: Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise him up. And if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
simplify: If anyone is sick, he should call the church leaders, who should pray over him and anoint him with oil in the Lord's name. When you are sick, ask your church leaders to pray with you and for you. The prayer offered in faith will restore the sick person, the Lord will raise him up, and any sins he has committed will be forgiven. God hears faithful prayer for the sick, and he can bring healing and forgiveness.

text: The LORD shall preserve you from all evil; He shall preserve your soul. The LORD shall preserve your going out and your coming in From this time forth, and even forevermore.
simplify: God will keep you from harm and look after your whole self, not just your body. You can trust him with your deepest needs, not only your outward safety. God watches over every part of your life, every coming and going, now and always. His care is not temporary but lasts forever.

text: By pride comes nothing but strife, But with the well-advised is wisdom.
simplify: Pride only stirs up quarrels, but people who are humble and calm have wisdom. It means letting go of pride keeps peace, while insisting on your own way starts fights.

text: Take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him. And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day returns to you, saying, "I repent,' you shall forgive him."
simplify: Jesus tells his followers to watch themselves and to confront a fellow believer who sins, but to forgive them if they repent. We should take sin seriously in each other's lives while being ready to forgive. Even if someone wrongs you repeatedly in one day, Jesus says to forgive them each time they say they are sorry. Forgiveness should not run out.

text: A merry heart does good, like medicine, But a broken spirit dries the bones.
simplify: A cheerful heart is good medicine for the body, but a broken spirit drains your strength. It means take care of your inner joy and encourage others, because attitude affects health.

text: I, therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you to walk worthy of the calling with which you were called, with all lowliness and gentleness, with longsuffering, bearing with one another in love, endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
simplify: Paul, writing as a prisoner, urges readers to live in a way that matches the calling God gave them. Your everyday life should reflect what God has called you to be. Be humble, gentle, and patient, bearing with one another's faults because you love them. Treat the people around you with quiet kindness even when it's hard. Work hard to stay united in peace, keeping the harmony the Spirit gives. Don't let small conflicts break the bond between you and others.

text: Therefore I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, for kings and all who are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and reverence.
simplify: Paul wants the church to pray for everyone, asking God for help and thanking him for people. This means no one is left out of our prayers, even people we don't know. He especially wants prayer for rulers and leaders, so that society stays peaceful and we can live calmly and honor God. Praying for those in power is part of a faithful life.

text: This is my comfort in my affliction, For Your word has given me life.
simplify: When he's suffering, God's words comfort him and keep him going. It means God's word can sustain us in hard times.

text: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil, and release those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
simplify: Since the children share flesh and blood, he too shared in it, so that by his death he might destroy the one who holds the power of death, the devil. Jesus' death breaks the devil's grip on us. He did this to free those who were held in slavery all their lives by the fear of death. The reader need no longer be enslaved by that fear.

text: Do you see a man who excels in his work? He will stand before kings; He will not stand before unknown men.
simplify: Someone skilled at their work will serve before kings, not stay among ordinary people. Doing your work well brings honor and opens doors.

text: And when you pray, do not use vain repetitions as the heathen do. For they think that they will be heard for their many words.
simplify: Don't pile up empty words in prayer, thinking God will listen because you talk a lot. More words don't make a better prayer.

text: The LORD will perfect that which concerns me; Your mercy, O LORD, endures forever; Do not forsake the works of Your hands.
simplify: David is confident that the Lord will finish what he has started in his life, and he asks God not to abandon the work he has made. This means God's faithful love means he completes what he begins in you, so you can rest in that.

text: Therefore I say to you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little."
simplify: Jesus explains that her great love shows she understands how much she has been forgiven, while someone who thinks they need little forgiveness shows little love. The point is that realizing our need for forgiveness produces gratitude.

text: And do not lead us into temptation, But deliver us from the evil one. For Yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen.
simplify: Ask God not to lead you into testing but to keep you safe from the Evil One. You're asking for protection in the face of temptation and evil.

text: Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your call and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble; for so an entrance will be supplied to you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
simplify: Peter urges his readers to make their calling and election sure by living this way. Doing so keeps them from stumbling and gives them confidence in their standing with God. Living this way opens the door wide into Christ's eternal kingdom. It is not about earning salvation but about walking steadily toward the welcome God has prepared.

text: And if it seems evil to you to serve the LORD, choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."
simplify: Joshua puts the choice plainly: serve the old gods, serve the gods of the land, or serve the Lord, and he states that he and his family will serve the Lord. Each person has to decide whom they will follow.

text: Truly the signs of an apostle were accomplished among you with all perseverance, in signs and wonders and mighty deeds.
simplify: Paul points out that the marks of a true apostle—signs, wonders, and mighty works—were done among the Corinthians with quiet strength. This tells the reader that genuine ministry is confirmed by real evidence, not just claims.

text: For "whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved."
simplify: Everyone who calls on the Lord's name will be saved. Salvation is available to anyone who turns to him, no matter who they are.

text: Now I say that Jesus Christ has become a servant to the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made to the fathers, and that the Gentiles might glorify God for His mercy, as it is written: "For this reason I will confess to You among the Gentiles, And sing to Your name."
simplify: Christ became a servant to the Jewish people to show that God keeps the promises he made to their ancestors. God's promises are reliable, and Christ came to fulfill them. Christ also came so that non-Jewish people could praise God for his mercy, just as Scripture says. God's mercy reaches people of every background, so praise him for it.

text: Cause me to hear Your lovingkindness in the morning, For in You do I trust; Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, For I lift up my soul to You.
simplify: Ask God to show up in the morning, while you are listening. He answers with steady love.

text: But as it is written: "Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, Nor have entered into the heart of man The things which God has prepared for those who love Him."
simplify: Paul quotes Scripture to say that no eye, ear, or human heart has imagined what God has prepared for those who love him. It means God's good plans for his people are beyond anything we can picture.

text: My son, eat honey because it is good, And the honeycomb which is sweet to your taste; So shall the knowledge of wisdom be to your soul; If you have found it, there is a prospect, And your hope will not be cut off.
simplify: Honey is good and sweet to eat. This is a simple picture of something pleasant and worth having. In the same way, make wisdom your goal; if you have it, you'll have a future and your hope won't be cut off. Wisdom pays off in the long run.

text: We love Him because He first loved us.
simplify: We love because he loved us first. Our love is a response, never the starting point.

text: The LORD is my strength and song, And He has become my salvation.
simplify: The Lord gives the writer strength, a reason to sing, and rescue from danger. God himself is the source of your courage and your safety.

text: Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
simplify: Right living grows like a crop in the soil of peace, and it is harvested by those who work to make peace. If you want good things to grow, be a person who makes peace rather than conflict.

text: Behold, I will bring it health and healing; I will heal them and reveal to them the abundance of peace and truth.
simplify: God promises to heal the city and restore its health, giving the people lasting peace and security. No matter how broken things are, God can bring healing and wholeness.

text: The LORD will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace."
simplify: You do not have to fight this battle alone. God will handle what you cannot; your part is to stay calm and let him work.

text: Your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, "This is the way, walk in it," Whenever you turn to the right hand Or whenever you turn to the left.
simplify: God promises a voice behind them guiding them to turn the right way when they are unsure. It means God actively guides those who are willing to listen.

text: And forgive us our sins, For we also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. And do not lead us into temptation, But deliver us from the evil one."
simplify: This asks God to forgive our sins in the same measure that we forgive those who owe us, and to keep us from being overcome by temptation. It means our own willingness to forgive is tied to how we ask for forgiveness.

text: "These things I have spoken to you, that My joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be full.
simplify: Jesus says all this so his joy can be in you and your joy can be full. This means his teaching is meant to give you complete, lasting joy, not to weigh you down.

text: If you abide in Me, and My words abide in you, you will ask what you desire, and it shall be done for you.
simplify: If you remain in Jesus and his words remain in you, you can ask for anything and it will be done. This means prayer becomes powerful when your life is deeply shaped by Jesus' teaching.

text: Continue earnestly in prayer, being vigilant in it with thanksgiving; meanwhile praying also for us, that God would open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in chains, that I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak.
simplify: Keep on praying at all times, staying alert and thankful as you do. Prayer should be a steady habit in your life, not just something for emergencies. Paul asks them to pray that God will open a door for the message about Christ to be preached, even though he is in chains for it. Pray for opportunities for God's word to spread, including through people who are suffering for it. Paul wants to explain the message clearly, as he should. Pray that those who speak about Christ will say it plainly and well.

text: The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, And saves such as have a contrite spirit.
simplify: God is closest when you are most broken. A crushed heart is not a place he avoids.

text: Say to those who are fearful-hearted, "Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God will come with vengeance, With the recompense of God; He will come and save you."
simplify: Tell frightened people to be brave because God is coming to rescue them and make things right. It means fear does not get the last word, since God himself comes to save.

text: By humility and the fear of the LORD Are riches and honor and life.
simplify: Being humble and respecting God brings honor, a good life, and what you truly need. True reward comes from a humble heart, not from chasing things.

text: Moreover the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still shut up in the court of the prison, saying, "Thus says the LORD who made it, the LORD who formed it to establish it (the LORD is His name): "Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you great and mighty things, which you do not know.'
simplify: God spoke to Jeremiah a second time while he was locked up in the guardhouse. Even when we are confined or in hard circumstances, God can still reach us and speak to us. God identifies himself as the one who made and established everything, and his name is the Lord. The God who speaks is the same God who created all things, so his words can be trusted. God invites you to ask, and promises to answer with things you could not work out alone. Prayer is meant to be specific.

text: And those who know Your name will put their trust in You; For You, LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
simplify: Those who know God trust him because he has never abandoned those who wait for him. It encourages the reader to trust God, who keeps his promises.

text: Brethren, I do not count myself to have apprehended; but one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind and reaching forward to those things which are ahead, I press toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.
simplify: Paul is honest that he hasn't reached the goal, so he focuses on one thing: forgetting what is behind and reaching forward. We should not be stuck in past failures or successes but keep moving toward God's call. Paul runs toward the goal to win the prize of God's upward call in Christ Jesus. The Christian life is like a race with a real reward waiting at the end.

text: For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world--our faith.
simplify: Everything that comes from God can win the victory over the world's pull away from him. The way we win that victory is by trusting God.

text: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light; who once were not a people but are now the people of God, who had not obtained mercy but now have obtained mercy.
simplify: You are a chosen people, a holy nation, and a royal priesthood belonging completely to God. Your purpose is to tell others about the wonderful things God did by bringing you from darkness into his marvelous light. At one time you weren't considered God's people, but now you are. You hadn't received mercy before, but now God has shown you great mercy.

text: Your wife shall be like a fruitful vine In the very heart of your house, Your children like olive plants All around your table.
simplify: Your home will be full of life, with a loving wife and children gathered around you like healthy plants. It pictures family as one of God's good gifts to be thankful for.

text: Now God worked unusual miracles by the hands of Paul, so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were brought from his body to the sick, and the diseases left them and the evil spirits went out of them.
simplify: God did extraordinary miracles through Paul. The power was God's, not Paul's. Even cloths that had touched Paul's body were taken to the sick, and their illnesses left and evil spirits went out. God chose to work in an unusual way to show his care for suffering people.

text: The Lord is not slack concerning His promise, as some count slackness, but is longsuffering toward us, not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance.
simplify: The Lord isn't late; he is patiently giving people time to turn from their wrong ways because he doesn't want anyone destroyed. His waiting is mercy, not neglect.

text: And whatever you ask in My name, that I will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
simplify: Jesus promises to answer requests made in his name, so that the Father gets the glory. Praying in his name means asking in line with who he is, with the aim of honoring God rather than just getting your way.

text: It is better to trust in the LORD Than to put confidence in man.
simplify: It is safer to trust the Lord than to rely on human beings. People will let you down, but God is dependable.

text: So he cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree. When he cast it into the waters, the waters were made sweet. There He made a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them, and said, "If you diligently heed the voice of the LORD your God and do what is right in His sight, give ear to His commandments and keep all His statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have brought on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you."
simplify: God answered Moses' prayer by showing him a tree that made the water drinkable. Here God also gave the people a rule and tested their trust in him. God promised that if the people listened to him and obeyed, he would keep them from the diseases he had brought on Egypt. He calls himself their healer, so the reader sees that obedience and trust bring life.

text: You are my hiding place and my shield; I hope in Your word.
simplify: God is his hiding place and shield from danger, and his hope is in God's word. When you feel threatened, God himself is your protection, and his word is your hope.

text: He who does not love does not know God, for God is love.
simplify: God is love, so a life without love does not know him. Love is evidence, not just sentiment.

text: The LORD will give strength to His people; The LORD will bless His people with peace.
simplify: The same powerful God gives his people strength and peace. The reader is encouraged that God's might is used to bless and calm those who belong to him.

text: Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom also we have access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
simplify: Because faith has made us right with God, we can now live at peace with him, and Jesus is the one who made that possible. For you, this means you don't have to feel God is against you anymore. Through Jesus we have gained access by faith to this grace we now stand in, and we can be glad as we look forward to sharing God's glory. For you, this means your standing with God is secure and your future is bright.

text: When I shut up heaven and there is no rain, or command the locusts to devour the land, or send pestilence among My people, if My people who are called by My name will humble themselves, and pray and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin and heal their land.
simplify: God describes times when he may withhold rain, send locusts, or bring disease on the land. Hard times can come, and God is sovereign even over them. If God's people humble themselves, pray, seek him, and turn from their wrong ways, he will hear from heaven, forgive them, and restore their land. This is a clear promise that humble repentance brings God's forgiveness and healing.

text: And he said: "The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer; The God of my strength, in whom I will trust; My shield and the horn of my salvation, My stronghold and my refuge; My Savior, You save me from violence. I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; So shall I be saved from my enemies.
simplify: David calls the Lord his rock, his fortress, and the one who saves him. For the reader, it means God is a solid, safe place to depend on. David piles up pictures of God as his protector, shield, and hiding place. It means you can trust God to keep you safe from people who mean you harm. David says he will call out to the Lord, who deserves praise, and God will save him from his enemies. It encourages the reader to pray to God when others are against them.

text: Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
simplify: What looks like foolishness or weakness in God is still far wiser and stronger than anything humans have. It encourages the reader to trust God's ways even when they don't make sense to them.

text: Blessed are the merciful, For they shall obtain mercy.
simplify: Those who show mercy and kindness to others are blessed because they will receive mercy. It means the way you treat others comes back to you in God's dealings with you.

text: Then he said to them, "Go your way, eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared; for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not sorrow, for the joy of the LORD is your strength."
simplify: Joy is not a luxury here; it is strength. God's joy carries you through days you could not carry on your own.

text: A wrathful man stirs up strife, But he who is slow to anger allays contention.
simplify: A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but someone slow to anger calms a quarrel. Being patient can stop a fight before it starts.

text: Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever.
simplify: God is good and his love never stops, so thanking him is always the right response. You can praise him today knowing his kindness toward you won't run out.

text: Therefore you now have sorrow; but I will see you again and your heart will rejoice, and your joy no one will take from you.
simplify: They were sad then, but Jesus would see them again and their joy would be permanent. It means the joy Jesus gives cannot be taken away by anyone.

text: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God; because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
simplify: Not everyone who claims to speak for God is really from him, so test what they say. Check teachings against the truth instead of believing them just because they sound spiritual.

text: The blessing of the LORD makes one rich, And He adds no sorrow with it.
simplify: When God blesses you with wealth, it does not come with added sorrow, and hard work alone cannot match it. Receive good things with gratitude rather than anxiety.

text: Watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."
simplify: Jesus tells his friends to stay awake and pray so they won't give in to temptation. It's a reminder that we may sincerely want to do right, but our weak human nature needs God's help through prayer.

text: Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever.
simplify: Give thanks to the Lord because he is good and his mercy never ends. God's kindness is constant, which is a steady reason for gratitude.

text: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
simplify: God promises a new heart and a new spirit, replacing their hard, stone-like heart with a soft, living one. It means deep inner change is God's gift, not something they must produce alone.

text: Resist him, steadfast in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings are experienced by your brotherhood in the world.
simplify: Resist the devil by standing firm in your faith, remembering that believers everywhere face the same kinds of struggles. You are not alone in your suffering.

text: But as God has distributed to each one, as the Lord has called each one, so let him walk. And so I ordain in all the churches.
simplify: Paul's rule for all churches is that people should live out their calling in the situation God placed them in. For the reader, you don't need to change your circumstances to serve God faithfully where you are.

text: Behold, children are a heritage from the LORD, The fruit of the womb is a reward. Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, So are the children of one's youth. Happy is the man who has his quiver full of them; They shall not be ashamed, But shall speak with their enemies in the gate.
simplify: Children are a gift from God, not just something people produce on their own. Parents should see their kids as a blessing given to them. Children born to young parents are like arrows in a warrior's hand—strong and ready to be used. They are a source of strength and purpose for the family. A man with many children is blessed, and they will stand up for him when trouble comes. Having a family that supports you is a real advantage and a reason to be glad.

text: Therefore they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who was bearing witness to the word of His grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
simplify: They stayed a long time and kept speaking boldly, and God backed up their message with miracles. It means God can confirm his message through ordinary people who trust him.

text: For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.
simplify: God made us new in Christ Jesus to do good works that he had already prepared for us. It means good works are the result of God's work in you, not the price of your salvation.

text: The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly.
simplify: The thief takes life; Jesus gives it in abundance. Abundance means full, not merely longer.

text: For we have become partakers of Christ if we hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast to the end, while it is said: "Today, if you will hear His voice, Do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion."
simplify: For we share in Christ if we hold firmly to the confidence we had at first all the way to the end. As it says: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as when they provoked him.

text: Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
simplify: When people treat you badly, respond by asking God to bless them rather than cursing them.

text: "And now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in You.
simplify: Having seen how fleeting life is, David says his only real hope is in the Lord. It invites the reader to place their hope in God rather than in things that do not last.

text: But You, O Lord, are a God full of compassion, and gracious, Longsuffering and abundant in mercy and truth.
simplify: God is compassionate, forgiving, slow to anger, and full of mercy and truth. You can rely on God's patience and kindness when you fail.

text: It is God who arms me with strength, And makes my way perfect.
simplify: God gives David strength and makes his path straight. It means God equips ordinary people to walk steadily through life.

text: Let him turn away from evil and do good; Let him seek peace and pursue it.
simplify: Turn away from evil and do good; actively hunt for peace and pursue it. Peace doesn't just happen—you have to go after it.

text: "So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take sickness away from the midst of you.
simplify: Worship the Lord your God, and he will bless your food and water and take sickness away from among you. Putting God first brings blessing and health.

text: Keep me as the apple of Your eye; Hide me under the shadow of Your wings, From the wicked who oppress me, From my deadly enemies who surround me.
simplify: David asks God to guard him like something very precious and to shelter him under his wings. It means we can ask God for close protection when we feel vulnerable. David asks to be kept safe from violent enemies who surround him and want him dead. It means we can bring real threats and fears to God and ask for safety.

text: Where there is no counsel, the people fall; But in the multitude of counselors there is safety.
simplify: Without good advice a people fall, but with many wise counselors they are safe. Seek wise advice before making big decisions.

text: And as it is appointed for men to die once, but after this the judgment, so Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many. To those who eagerly wait for Him He will appear a second time, apart from sin, for salvation.
simplify: Just as people are appointed to die once, and after that comes judgment, so Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time—not to deal with sin again—to bring salvation to those eagerly waiting for him. His first coming dealt with sin; his second brings final salvation.

text: Therefore we also, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which so easily ensnares us, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith, who for the joy that was set before Him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
simplify: Drop the weight and run your race, looking at Jesus. He already ran it.

text: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for Him; Do not fret because of him who prospers in his way, Because of the man who brings wicked schemes to pass. Cease from anger, and forsake wrath; Do not fret--it only causes harm. For evildoers shall be cut off; But those who wait on the LORD, They shall inherit the earth.
simplify: Be still and wait patiently for God instead of getting worked up when someone's scheming seems to pay off. Quiet trust is the better path.
