Let go of anger and resentment, because nursing it only leads you into doing wrong yourself. Those who do evil will be removed, but people who trust God will inherit the land. Your future is secure in him.

text: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.
simplify: Through Jesus, we should continually offer praise to God, which is like a sacrifice. Speaking well of his name and thanking him is the offering he wants from us.

text: "I, even I, am He who comforts you. Who are you that you should be afraid Of a man who will die, And of the son of a man who will be made like grass?
simplify: God himself says he is the one who comforts them. He asks why they are so afraid of mere humans, who are as temporary as grass and will soon fade away.

text: Peace I leave with you, My peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
simplify: His peace is not the kind the world gives, which depends on circumstances. You can be steady while things are not.

text: "Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy and where thieves break in and steal; but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
simplify: Don't pile up wealth here on earth, where it wears out and thieves can steal it. Earthly treasure doesn't last. Store up treasure in heaven, where nothing wears out and no thief can take it. Invest in what lasts forever. Your heart follows your treasure, so where you put your wealth shows what you really care about. What you value most will shape your life.

text: Now this is the confidence that we have in Him, that if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us.
simplify: We can be confident that if we ask for something that matches what God wants, he hears us. Prayer is not wishful thinking but a real conversation with a listening God.

text: Therefore, in all things He had to be made like His brethren, that He might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
simplify: So he had to become like his brothers and sisters in every way, to be a merciful and faithful high priest in God's service, making atonement for the sins of the people. The reader has a high priest who truly understands them.

text: Then He who sat on the throne said, "Behold, I make all things new." And He said to me, "Write, for these words are true and faithful."
simplify: God himself promises to make everything new and tells John to write it down because it is certain. You can trust this promise even when life still feels old and worn.

text: Blessed is the man who endures temptation; for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord has promised to those who love Him.
simplify: The person who endures testing is blessed, because God will give the crown of life to those who love him. The reader can hold on in trials with the promise of life ahead.

text: You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, that whatever you ask the Father in My name He may give you.
simplify: You didn't choose Jesus; he chose you and appointed you to go and bear lasting fruit, so the Father will give you whatever you ask in his name. This means your purpose comes from his choice of you, and your prayers are backed by that calling.

text: My son, keep your father's command, And do not forsake the law of your mother.
simplify: Listen to your father's instruction and don't forget what your mother taught you. Their guidance is worth keeping.

text: "Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth, a Man attested by God to you by miracles, wonders, and signs which God did through Him in your midst, as you yourselves also know-- Him, being delivered by the determined purpose and foreknowledge of God, you have taken by lawless hands, have crucified, and put to death; whom God raised up, having loosed the pains of death, because it was not possible that He should be held by it.
simplify: Peter told the people of Israel to listen: Jesus of Nazareth was a man approved by God, proven by the miracles and wonders God did through him among them, which they themselves saw. It means Jesus' identity was backed up by public evidence, not just claims. Jesus was handed over according to God's plan and foreknowledge, and the people put him to death by the hands of lawless men. It means both God's purpose and human guilt were involved in the cross, so the reader sees that evil was real even while God was working. But God raised Jesus back to life, freeing him from the pain of death, because death could not hold him. It means death was defeated, and the reader can have hope that death is not the final word.

text: But what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart" (that is, the word of faith which we preach): that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
simplify: The message of faith is close and accessible, right there in your mouth and heart. You don't have to search far; the good news is near you and can be believed and spoken. Believe in your heart and say it with your mouth. Faith is not meant to stay secret.

text: Therefore do not cast away your confidence, which has great reward. For you have need of endurance, so that after you have done the will of God, you may receive the promise: "For yet a little while, And He who is coming will come and will not tarry.
simplify: So don't throw away your confidence; it will be richly rewarded. Giving up now forfeits a real reward. You need to keep doing God's will and patiently endure, so you can receive what he promised. Patience is part of receiving the promise. In just a little while, the one who is coming will come and won't delay. The wait is real but limited—he is coming.

text: For assuredly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, "Be removed and be cast into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that those things he says will be done, he will have whatever he says.
simplify: Jesus said that anyone who tells a mountain to throw itself into the sea, without doubting in their heart but believing what they say will happen, will get what they ask for. He was teaching that real faith in God is powerful.

text: Now to Him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us, to Him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
simplify: God can do more than you would even think to ask. Your imagination is the smaller limit. Paul ends by giving glory to God in the church and in Christ Jesus for all generations forever. It means the church's purpose is to honor God, and that honor never ends.

text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, But when the desire comes, it is a tree of life.
simplify: Hope that keeps being delayed makes the heart sick, but getting what you long for brings fresh life. It means waiting can be painful, and fulfilled hope is deeply refreshing.

text: Beloved, let us love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves is born of God and knows God.
simplify: Love one another, because love comes from God and marks everyone who is truly his child. If you know God, love for others should be a natural part of your life.

text: For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is loyal to Him. In this you have done foolishly; therefore from now on you shall have wars."
simplify: God is always watching, ready to strengthen people whose hearts are fully his, and Hanani told Asa he had acted foolishly and would face wars from then on. God looks for wholehearted trust, and our choices have real consequences.

text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.
simplify: Fruit is grown, not manufactured. These are what God's Spirit produces in a life over time.

text: Brethren, if a man is overtaken in any trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself lest you also be tempted.
simplify: If someone is caught doing wrong, those who follow the Spirit should gently help them back on track, remembering they could fall too. It means correcting others with kindness, not pride, because you are not immune to temptation.

text: So we may boldly say: "The LORD is my helper; I will not fear. What can man do to me?"
simplify: Because the Lord is our helper, we can say with confidence that we will not be afraid. No human being can ultimately do anything that God does not allow.

text: Wisdom is the principal thing; Therefore get wisdom. And in all your getting, get understanding.
simplify: The most important thing about wisdom is actually getting it, even if it costs you everything. For the reader, it means wisdom is worth more than anything else you could spend on.

text: For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.
simplify: God made Christ, who knew no sin, to be sin for us, so that in him we might become God's righteousness. The reader can receive a right standing with God as a gift, because Christ took our sin in our place.

text: Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
simplify: Rejoice with people who are happy and grieve with people who are sad—truly share in their lives.

text: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
simplify: Keep waiting calmly and make your hearts strong, because the Lord's coming is near. Because Jesus is coming soon, you can stay steady and not give up.

text: For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be refused if it is received with thanksgiving; for it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
simplify: Everything God created is good, and nothing should be rejected if we receive it with gratitude. It means we can enjoy God's gifts thankfully rather than treating ordinary things as evil. Food and other gifts are set apart for holy use when we remember God's word and pray over them. It encourages us to thank God and pray before enjoying what he provides.

text: Sing, O heavens! Be joyful, O earth! And break out in singing, O mountains! For the LORD has comforted His people, And will have mercy on His afflicted.
simplify: Heaven, earth, and mountains are called to sing because God comforts his people and shows mercy to the crushed. It invites the reader to celebrate God's care for the hurting.

text: You who fear the LORD, trust in the LORD; He is their help and their shield.
simplify: Everyone who worships the Lord is urged to trust him, because he helps and shields them. This invitation to trust God is open to all who honor him.

text: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, The Holy One of Israel: "I am the LORD your God, Who teaches you to profit, Who leads you by the way you should go.
simplify: The Lord, who defends Israel, says he is their God who teaches them what is best and guides them in the right way. The reader is invited to trust God's teaching as loving guidance.

text: The LORD is near to all who call upon Him, To all who call upon Him in truth.
simplify: God is near to everyone who calls on him honestly. He is not far from the person who actually wants him.

text: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
simplify: If God is on your side, the opposition loses its case. You are not alone in the argument.

text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also He has put eternity in their hearts, except that no one can find out the work that God does from beginning to end.
simplify: God makes everything fitting in its time, yet he has kept people from fully understanding his plan from beginning to end. You can trust God's timing even when you can't see the whole picture.

text: And those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
simplify: Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. For you, it means you have said no to your sinful nature and should keep saying no to it.

text: Therefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Christ Jesus, who was faithful to Him who appointed Him, as Moses also was faithful in all His house.
simplify: Since you are set apart for God and share in a heavenly calling, fix your attention on Jesus, who is the apostle and high priest of our faith. Jesus was faithful to God who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in God's house.

text: He who troubles his own house will inherit the wind, And the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
simplify: Whoever brings trouble on their own household inherits nothing but wind, and the fool ends up serving the wise. Do not wreck your home with foolishness, because folly leads to loss and servitude.

text: And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and signs among the people.
simplify: Stephen, full of grace and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people. It means God was working powerfully through an ordinary servant chosen to handle food distribution.

text: And truly Jesus did many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book; but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in His name.
simplify: Jesus did many other miraculous signs that aren't written down in this book. The Gospel doesn't claim to record everything, just what's needed. The accounts were written so readers would believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life through him. The whole point of the book is to bring you to faith and to life.

text: All your children shall be taught by the LORD, And great shall be the peace of your children.
simplify: God says he will teach all his people, and their children will enjoy great peace. The reader can look for God's own teaching and for peace that reaches their family.

text: Jesus answered and said to him, "Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
simplify: Jesus told him that to see God's kingdom, a person must be born all over again. This means a fresh start from God is needed, not just being religious.

text: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD his God.
simplify: Jotham grew strong because he made the Lord his guide in everything he did. The reader learns that lasting strength comes from depending on God, not just from hard work or good plans.

text: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts, and always be ready to give a defense to everyone who asks you a reason for the hope that is in you, with meekness and fear; having a good conscience, that when they defame you as evildoers, those who revile your good conduct in Christ may be ashamed.
simplify: Set Christ apart as Lord in your heart and always be ready to explain the hope you have—respectfully and humbly. Know why you believe so you can answer kindly when asked. Keep a clear conscience so that those who insult your good Christian life will end up ashamed of their slander. Live so your accusers have nothing real to hold against you.

text: The LORD has appeared of old to me, saying: "Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love; Therefore with lovingkindness I have drawn you.
simplify: God says his love for his people has always been and always will be, and that love is what drew them to himself. For the reader, it means you are loved with a lasting love, not a temporary feeling.

text: I will love You, O LORD, my strength. The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer; My God, my strength, in whom I will trust; My shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
simplify: David says he will love the Lord, who is his strength, after God rescued him from all his enemies, including Saul. It invites the reader to love God as the one who gives them strength. God is not one help among many; he is rock, fortress and rescue. There is somewhere solid to stand.

text: When a man's ways please the LORD, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
simplify: When your life pleases God, he can even calm the people who are against you. Focus on living rightly and trust God to handle your enemies.

text: The LORD will strengthen him on his bed of illness; You will sustain him on his sickbed.
simplify: When you are sick and lying in pain, God himself strengthens and supports you. He can turn your deepest sorrow into renewed strength.

text: The LORD is good, A stronghold in the day of trouble; And He knows those who trust in Him.
simplify: Even while describing judgment, this verse says God is good and a safe shelter in hard times, and he knows and protects those who trust him. The reader can run to God for safety rather than try to hide from him.

text: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
simplify: Let Christ's message dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing to God with gratitude. Fill your life with his word and let it overflow in worship together.

text: Or do you despise the riches of His goodness, forbearance, and longsuffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?
simplify: God has been patient and kind with us, waiting for us to change, and that kindness is meant to lead us to turn from wrong. It means we shouldn't treat God's patience as if it doesn't matter.

text: Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.
simplify: They had not yet asked for anything in Jesus' name, and he told them to ask so their joy would be complete. It means prayer is meant to fill you with joy, not just get answers.

text: Therefore be patient, brethren, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, waiting patiently for it until it receives the early and latter rain.
simplify: Be patient until the Lord comes, the way a farmer waits patiently for the rains and the harvest. Waiting for God's timing takes patience, and that patience is part of trusting him.

text: I will praise the name of God with a song, And will magnify Him with thanksgiving.
simplify: He promises to praise God with a song and to thank him for what he has done. It means praise is a fitting response to God, even while we are still waiting for rescue.

text: And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away."
simplify: Every tear wiped away, death gone, pain over. The end of the story is not what it looks like now.

text: But now, thus says the LORD, who created you, O Jacob, And He who formed you, O Israel: "Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; You are Mine.
simplify: God tells his people not to be afraid because he made them and claims them as his own, calling each by name. You can face fear knowing you belong to the one who made you and stands up for you.

text: Better is a little with righteousness, Than vast revenues without justice.
simplify: A small amount gained honestly is better than a large amount gained by cheating. Be content with less if it means keeping your integrity.

text: But I say to you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who spitefully use you and persecute you, that you may be sons of your Father in heaven; for He makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust.
simplify: Jesus tells us to love the people who oppose us and pray for those who treat us badly. This is a hard command, but it shows real love instead of revenge. By loving even your enemies you show that you belong to God, who gives sun and rain to both good and bad people. God is kind to everyone, and he wants his children to be like him.

text: Vindicate me, O LORD, For I have walked in my integrity. I have also trusted in the LORD; I shall not slip. Examine me, O LORD, and prove me; Try my mind and my heart. For Your lovingkindness is before my eyes, And I have walked in Your truth.
simplify: David asks God to examine his life because he has tried to live honestly and has trusted God to keep him steady. It invites the reader to live with integrity and to trust God to be the judge of their life. David asks God to test him thoroughly, like weighing something on a scale or purifying metal with fire, to see what is really in his mind and heart. It means being willing to let God show you the truth about yourself, even when it is uncomfortable. David keeps God's faithful love in view and has tried to live by God's truth. It reminds the reader that remembering God's kindness helps a person stay on the right path.

text: "For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; And the former shall not be remembered or come to mind.
simplify: God promises to create new heavens and a new earth, with the former things completely forgotten. It means God's ultimate plan is full renewal, not just patching up the old.

text: Your word I have hidden in my heart, That I might not sin against You.
simplify: The writer has stored God's words deep in his heart so he won't sin against God. It tells the reader that memorizing and treasuring God's word helps guard against doing wrong.

text: And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose.
simplify: God works everything together for good for those who love him. Not that everything is good, but that nothing is wasted.

text: A wise son makes a father glad, But a foolish man despises his mother.
simplify: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man treats his mother with contempt. Let your choices bring honor to your parents.

text: Now, Lord, look on their threats, and grant to Your servants that with all boldness they may speak Your word, by stretching out Your hand to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done through the name of Your holy Servant Jesus."
simplify: They asked God to notice the threats and to give them boldness to keep preaching his word. Instead of praying for safety, they prayed for courage. They asked God to stretch out his hand to heal and to do signs and wonders through the name of Jesus. They wanted God's power to be seen so people would believe.

text: And I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish; neither shall anyone snatch them out of My hand.
simplify: He gives them eternal life; they will never be destroyed, and no one can snatch them out of his hand. It means those who belong to Jesus are permanently safe.

text: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.
simplify: God gives power, love and self-control, not fear. If it is fear, it is not from him.

text: Let your conduct be without covetousness; be content with such things as you have. For He Himself has said, "I will never leave you nor forsake you."
simplify: Be content with what you have; he will not leave you. Contentment rests on his promise, not your stock.

text: So then, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath; for the wrath of man does not produce the righteousness of God.
simplify: Be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry. The reader is given practical guidance for everyday relationships. Human anger does not produce the righteous life God wants. The reader is warned that losing their temper does not achieve God's purposes.

text: I wait for the LORD, my soul waits, And in His word I do hope.
simplify: The writer waits for the Lord with his whole heart and puts his hope in what God has promised. Waiting on God is worth it because his word can be trusted.

text: "Therefore know that the LORD your God, He is God, the faithful God who keeps covenant and mercy for a thousand generations with those who love Him and keep His commandments; and He repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them. He will not be slack with him who hates Him; He will repay him to his face.
simplify: Israel should be certain that the Lord is God, faithful and merciful, keeping his word for a thousand generations to those who love him and keep his commands. The reader can trust that God keeps his promises across generations. God repays those who hate him with open destruction and shows them no mercy. The reader is reminded that rejecting God is serious and brings real consequences.

text: O God, You are more awesome than Your holy places. The God of Israel is He who gives strength and power to His people. Blessed be God!
simplify: God is awe-inspiring in his holy place and gives strength to his people. The psalm ends with praise, and the reader is invited to trust God for strength and to praise him.

text: Deceit is in the heart of those who devise evil, But counselors of peace have joy.
simplify: People who plan evil carry deceit in their hearts, but those who work for peace find joy. Aim for peace with others, because that path leads to happiness.

text: But to you who fear My name The Sun of Righteousness shall arise With healing in His wings; And you shall go out And grow fat like stall-fed calves.
simplify: For those who honor God, that same day brings healing and new life, like sunrise after darkness. It means you can look forward with hope, because God's justice ends in joy for those who trust him.

text: As for God, His way is perfect; The word of the LORD is proven; He is a shield to all who trust in Him.
simplify: God's way is perfect, his word is proven true, and he shields everyone who trusts him. It means you can rely on God's character and promises.

text: For wisdom is a defense as money is a defense, But the excellence of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who have it.
simplify: Wisdom protects you the way money does, but wisdom is better because it keeps its owner alive. Both help, but wisdom matters more.

text: And when they had nothing with which to repay, he freely forgave them both. Tell Me, therefore, which of them will love him more?"
simplify: Neither person could pay, so the lender simply canceled both debts. Jesus asks which one would be more grateful and loving toward the man who freed them.

text: He who heeds the word wisely will find good, And whoever trusts in the LORD, happy is he.
simplify: Paying attention to good teaching brings benefit, and trusting God brings happiness. Listen to wise instruction and put your trust in the Lord.

text: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he endured as seeing Him who is invisible.
simplify: Moses left Egypt without being scared off by the king's anger, as though he could see the invisible God. Faith keeps going because it sees God even when he is unseen.

text: But I will sacrifice to You With the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay what I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD."
simplify: Jonah promises to thank God with a loud voice and to keep his promises, saying that rescue comes from the Lord. It means that our response to God's help should be gratitude and trust in him alone.

text: Show me a sign for good, That those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, Because You, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
simplify: David asks for a visible sign of God's goodness so his enemies will see it and be put to shame. You can ask God to show his goodness in ways that encourage you and silence those who oppose you.

text: You must not fear them, for the LORD your God Himself fights for you.'
simplify: Moses told the people not to fear their enemies because God himself would fight for them. The reader is reminded that courage rests on God's help, not on their own strength.

text: The generous soul will be made rich, And he who waters will also be watered himself.
simplify: Those who bless others will be blessed and satisfied, but those who curse will be cursed. Be generous with your kindness, because it comes back to you.

text: And if we know that He hears us, whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we have asked of Him.
simplify: Since we know he hears every request that is in line with his will, we can know he will answer. You can pray with confidence, not fear.

text: "Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his master made ruler over his household, to give them food in due season? Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.
simplify: Jesus describes a faithful, sensible servant whose master put him in charge of feeding the household. The question is whether you will faithfully do the work God has given you. That servant is blessed because his master finds him doing his job when he returns. It is good to be found faithfully doing what God has entrusted to you.

text: "Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
simplify: Ask, seek, knock: prayer is meant to keep going. God is not annoyed by persistence.

text: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil.
simplify: Sin belongs to the devil, who has been sinning from the start, and Jesus came to destroy the devil's work. It means sin is not your friend, and Jesus has the power to break it in your life.

text: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb and called me through His grace, to reveal His Son in me, that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately confer with flesh and blood, nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me; but I went to Arabia, and returned again to Damascus.
simplify: But God, who had set Paul apart even before he was born, chose in his kindness to act. It means God's plan for Paul's life was not an accident but a deliberate act of grace. God chose to reveal his Son in Paul so that Paul would tell the good news about Jesus to non-Jewish people. It means Paul's mission came straight from God, and he did not need to check with people first. Paul did not go to Jerusalem to consult the apostles who were there before him; instead he went to Arabia and later returned to Damascus. It means he followed God's leading rather than seeking human approval.

text: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is For brethren to dwell together in unity!
simplify: It is genuinely good and pleasant when people who belong together live in peace instead of fighting. You can enjoy that kind of harmony in your own family and community and treat it as something worth having.

text: And His name, through faith in His name, has made this man strong, whom you see and know. Yes, the faith which comes through Him has given him this perfect soundness in the presence of you all.
simplify: It was faith in the name of Jesus that made this man strong and completely well in front of everyone. The power came through trusting in Jesus, not through Peter.

text: I say to you that likewise there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance.
simplify: Jesus says heaven celebrates more over one sinner who turns back to God than over ninety-nine who think they don't need to. No one is too far gone for God to rejoice over.

text: The things which you learned and received and heard and saw in me, these do, and the God of peace will be with you.
simplify: Paul tells them to put into practice what they learned and saw in him, and promises God's peace will be with them. It means following good teaching in action brings God's presence into your life.

text: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High Shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the LORD, "He is my refuge and my fortress; My God, in Him I will trust."
simplify: Living close to God is its own shelter. He is a refuge, not just a last resort.

text: And Azariah the chief priest, from the house of Zadok, answered him and said, "Since the people began to bring the offerings into the house of the LORD, we have had enough to eat and have plenty left, for the LORD has blessed His people; and what is left is this great abundance."
simplify: Azariah the chief priest answered that ever since the people began bringing offerings, there had been more than enough food, because the Lord had blessed his people and left a great surplus. It means God's blessing showed up in practical abundance, and it reassures the reader that God's provision often exceeds what is strictly needed.

text: Let Your mercy, O LORD, be upon us, Just as we hope in You.
simplify: May your kindness be upon us, Lord, just as we wait for you. It means asking God for his mercy while continuing to trust and wait for him.

text: Greater love has no one than this, than to lay down one's life for his friends.
simplify: The greatest love a person can show is to give up their life for their friends. This means sacrificial love, putting others before yourself even at great cost, is the highest kind.

text: And he shall say to them, "Hear, O Israel: Today you are on the verge of battle with your enemies. Do not let your heart faint, do not be afraid, and do not tremble or be terrified because of them; for the LORD your God is He who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.'
simplify: The priest tells the people to be brave and not let panic take over when they face their enemies. The reader is reminded that courage is a choice we make even when fear is strong. The reason they need not fear is that God himself goes with them and fights on their behalf. The reader can trust that God is actively involved in their struggles, not distant from them.

text: For the mountains shall depart And the hills be removed, But My kindness shall not depart from you, Nor shall My covenant of peace be removed," Says the LORD, who has mercy on you.
simplify: Even if mountains and hills were to move, God says his love will not leave his people and his peace agreement will not break. The reader can rest in a love that is more solid than the most solid things on earth.

text: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.
simplify: Put God's kingdom first and the rest finds its place. Anxiety shrinks when the order is right.

text: I have set the LORD always before me; Because He is at my right hand I shall not be moved.
simplify: Keeping God in front of you keeps you steady. You will not be shaken when he is your centre.

text: For God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy to a man who is good in His sight; but to the sinner He gives the work of gathering and collecting, that he may give to him who is good before God. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
simplify: God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to those who please him, while sinners just pile up wealth for others to enjoy. It means God rewards those who follow him, and hoarding wealth is ultimately empty.

text: But if you had known what this means, "I desire mercy and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned the guiltless.
simplify: God cares more about mercy than about religious rituals, and if the Pharisees understood this they would not have condemned innocent people. Readers are reminded to show mercy rather than nitpick.

text: Happy are the people who are in such a state; Happy are the people whose God is the LORD!
simplify: David says a nation is truly happy when its life is ordered well and its God is the Lord. It means real happiness comes from belonging to God, not just from having plenty.

text: And Moses indeed was faithful in all His house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which would be spoken afterward, but Christ as a Son over His own house, whose house we are if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end.
simplify: Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house, pointing forward to what God would later say. But Christ is faithful as a son over God's house, and we are that house if we hold firmly to our confident hope to the end.

text: Oh, that men would give thanks to the LORD for His goodness, And for His wonderful works to the children of men!
simplify: People should thank God for his steady love and for the amazing things he does for them. Gratitude is the fitting response to being helped.

text: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me All the days of my life; And I will dwell in the house of the LORD Forever.
simplify: The Lord leads, provides and protects all the way through. Even in the darkest valley, you are not walking alone.

text: But even if you should suffer for righteousness' sake, you are blessed. "And do not be afraid of their threats, nor be troubled."
simplify: Even if you suffer for doing right, you are blessed; don't be afraid of what frightens others or let it shake you. Suffering for good doesn't mean God has abandoned you.

text: Honor the LORD with your possessions, And with the firstfruits of all your increase; So your barns will be filled with plenty, And your vats will overflow with new wine.
simplify: Honor God with your money and give him the first share of what you earn. It means putting God first with your resources, not just your words. If you do this, your barns will be full and your supplies will overflow. It means generosity toward God is pictured as leading to abundance and provision.

text: "So I say to you, ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
simplify: Jesus tells his followers to keep asking, keep seeking, and keep knocking, with the promise that these efforts will be answered. It's an invitation to persistent, confident prayer.

text: "Behold the proud, His soul is not upright in him; But the just shall live by his faith.
simplify: The proud person is not pleasing to God, but the honest person lives by trusting God. It means real life comes from faith and integrity, not from arrogance.

text: Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send Jesus Christ, who was preached to you before, whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began.
simplify: Peter called them to change their hearts and turn back to God so their sins could be wiped out and times of refreshment could come. Repentance is presented as the path to forgiveness and blessing. The goal of turning to God is that he may send the Messiah he had already appointed for them, namely Jesus. Their repentance was tied to God's future sending of Christ. Jesus must remain in heaven until the time when everything is restored, which God announced long ago through his holy prophets. There is a set future time for full restoration.

text: For all that is in the world--the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life--is not of the Father but is of the world.
simplify: The cravings of the body, the craving for what you see, and pride in what you have all come from the world, not from the Father. These desires don't come from God, so don't treat them as your guide.

text: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.
simplify: There is one body of believers and one Spirit, just as God gave you one shared hope. Remember you belong to one family with a common future. There is one Lord, one faith, and one baptism. What unites believers is far greater than what divides them. There is one God and Father over everyone, working through all and living in all. You are never outside his care or presence.

text: Wives, likewise, be submissive to your own husbands, that even if some do not obey the word, they, without a word, may be won by the conduct of their wives, when they observe your chaste conduct accompanied by fear.
simplify: Wives are told to follow their husbands' leadership so that a husband who ignores God's word might be won over by how his wife lives. Your everyday conduct can speak louder than any argument. The husband is won over by seeing his wife live a pure, respectful life shaped by her reverence for God. What you do matters more than what you say.

text: When Jesus heard that, He said, "This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified through it."
simplify: Jesus said this sickness would not end in death but would show God's glory and bring glory to God's Son. The reader learns that even bad situations can serve a bigger purpose.

text: And this is the testimony: that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. He who has the Son has life; he who does not have the Son of God does not have life.
simplify: God's testimony is that he has given us eternal life, and that life is found in his Son. You receive that life by having the Son. Whoever has the Son has real life; whoever does not have the Son does not have that life. It all hinges on your connection to Jesus.

text: "Again I say to you that if two of you agree on earth concerning anything that they ask, it will be done for them by My Father in heaven.
simplify: If two of you agree on earth about anything you ask, my Father in heaven will do it. Agreement in prayer matters to God.

text: Commit your way to the LORD, Trust also in Him, And He shall bring it to pass.
simplify: Hand your plans and your whole life over to God and trust him. He is the one who will make things work out.

text: Then your light shall break forth like the morning, Your healing shall spring forth speedily, And your righteousness shall go before you; The glory of the LORD shall be your rear guard.
simplify: If you do these things, light will break on you like dawn, your healing will come quickly, and God's glory will follow behind you. It means doing right by others brings God's light and restoration, and the reader can expect God to meet them as they act justly.

text: Why are you cast down, O my soul? And why are you disquieted within me? Hope in God; For I shall yet praise Him, The help of my countenance and my God.
simplify: He again challenges his downcast soul to hope in God and expects to praise him again as his help. It models turning despair toward hope, even when the feelings have not yet changed.

text: Oh, give thanks to the God of heaven! For His mercy endures forever.
simplify: Praise the God of heaven, because his love never ends. Thanking him is the right response to his constant faithfulness.

text: So Jesus answered and said to them, "Assuredly, I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but also if you say to this mountain, "Be removed and be cast into the sea,' it will be done.
simplify: Jesus told them that if they have faith without doubting, they could do even greater things, like telling a mountain to move into the sea. He was teaching that real faith in God is powerful.

text: Finally, brethren, farewell. Become complete. Be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace will be with you.
simplify: Paul closes by urging them to be joyful, grow toward maturity, encourage each other, agree with one another, and live in peace. It means these simple habits invite God's love and peace into our relationships.

text: Return to the stronghold, You prisoners of hope. Even today I declare That I will restore double to you.
simplify: The prisoners are called to return with hope, and God promises to restore them double what they lost. We can live with hope because God repays his people for their suffering.

text: The LORD is on my side; I will not fear. What can man do to me?
simplify: Because God is on the writer's side, he refuses to be afraid of what people might do to him. If God stands with you, human threats lose their power over you.

text: How much better to get wisdom than gold! And to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
simplify: Wisdom and understanding are worth far more than money. Spend your effort gaining wisdom, because it is more valuable than any wealth.

text: But go and learn what this means: "I desire mercy and not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance."
simplify: Jesus told them to learn that God wants mercy more than ritual, and that he came for sinners, not the self-righteous. God values compassion over outward religion.

text: My brethren, count it all joy when you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience.
simplify: Hard testing produces something comfort cannot. Joy here is not pretending; it is endurance with purpose.

text: And a servant of the Lord must not quarrel but be gentle to all, able to teach, patient, in humility correcting those who are in opposition, if God perhaps will grant them repentance, so that they may know the truth, and that they may come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, having been taken captive by him to do his will.
simplify: The Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but gentle toward everyone, able to teach, and patient when wronged. For the reader, it means represent Christ with gentleness and patience, especially under criticism. Correct opponents gently, in case God grants them repentance and knowledge of the truth. For the reader, it means how you correct others matters, because God may use your gentleness to change them. Then they may come to their senses and escape the devil's trap, having been captured by him to do his will. For the reader, it means gentle correction can free people from harmful patterns and bring them back to God.

text: Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever.
simplify: The writer calls everyone to praise the Lord because he is good and his love never stops. For you, it means you can thank God knowing his kindness toward you will not run out.

text: You shall increase my greatness, And comfort me on every side.
simplify: He believes God will restore him to honor and comfort him on every side. It expresses confidence that God's help brings comfort and renewal.

text: And Jesus answered and said to her, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about many things. But one thing is needed, and Mary has chosen that good part, which will not be taken away from her."
simplify: Jesus gently tells Martha that she is letting herself get worried and upset over too many tasks. It means we can wear ourselves out with busyness, and Jesus invites us to notice when our worry has grown out of proportion. Jesus says only a few things really matter, and Mary chose the one best thing by sitting and listening to him. It means time spent with Jesus is worth more than any task and is something no one can take from you.

text: It is like the dew of Hermon, Descending upon the mountains of Zion; For there the LORD commanded the blessing-- Life forevermore.
simplify: It is also like dew from Mount Hermon that waters the mountains of Zion, and God promised his blessing and lasting life right there. It means God's life and goodness flow to people who live together in peace, so peace is where his blessing is found.

text: Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
simplify: So we can come boldly to God's throne of grace, where we receive mercy and find grace to help us when we need it. God welcomes us to ask for help rather than staying away in fear.

text: Hear my prayer, O LORD, Give ear to my supplications! In Your faithfulness answer me, And in Your righteousness. Do not enter into judgment with Your servant, For in Your sight no one living is righteous.
simplify: David asks God to hear his prayer and answer him because God is faithful and good, not because David deserves it. We can pray boldly, trusting God's character rather than our own record. David admits that no one, himself included, could stand up to God's judgment. We should come to God honestly about our faults instead of pretending we are good enough on our own.

text: Then I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them, and take the stony heart out of their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh, that they may walk in My statutes and keep My judgments and do them; and they shall be My people, and I will be their God.
simplify: God promises to give them a new heart and a new spirit, replacing their hard, stone-like heart with a soft, living one. Real change comes as a gift from God, not from our own effort. The purpose of the new heart is that they will follow God's rules and obey his commands, and then they will truly be his people and he will be their God. Obedience flows from the heart God gives.

text: But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own desires and enticed.
simplify: Each person is tempted when their own desires draw them away and lure them. The reader is invited to look honestly at their own wants as the source of temptation.

text: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying: "Whom shall I send, And who will go for Us?" Then I said, "Here am I! Send me."
simplify: The Lord asked who would go on His behalf, and Isaiah immediately volunteered. This challenges the reader to be ready to answer God's call with willing obedience.

text: For I have known him, in order that he may command his children and his household after him, that they keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice, that the LORD may bring to Abraham what He has spoken to him."
simplify: God said he had chosen Abraham so he would teach his children and household to follow the Lord and do what is right. It shows that being chosen by God includes the responsibility to pass on faith to the next generation.

text: But I have a greater witness than John's; for the works which the Father has given Me to finish--the very works that I do--bear witness of Me, that the Father has sent Me.
simplify: Jesus said the witness he has is greater than John's: the works the Father gave him to do prove the Father sent him. Jesus' miracles were evidence of his mission from God.

text: And He Himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the whole world.
simplify: Jesus' death paid for our sins, and not just ours but the sins of the whole world. God's forgiveness is offered far more widely than just to you and your group.

text: "It shall come to pass That before they call, I will answer; And while they are still speaking, I will hear.
simplify: God says he will answer before they even call and listen while they are still praying. It means God is eager and quick to respond to his people.

text: But when Jesus heard it, He answered him, saying, "Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be made well."
simplify: Jesus told Jairus not to be afraid but to keep believing, and the girl would be healed. Fear and faith were set against each other, and Jesus called him to trust.

text: The LORD God is my strength; He will make my feet like deer's feet, And He will make me walk on my high hills. To the Chief Musician. With my stringed instruments.
simplify: God gives strength to stand on high places. He makes the climb possible, not painless.

text: The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear Him, In those who hope in His mercy.
simplify: God delights in those who honor him and rely on his kindness. It means your hope in his mercy actually pleases him.

text: In this is love, not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins.
simplify: Real love began with God, not with us: he loved us first and sent his Son to deal with our sins. We don't earn his love; we receive it.

text: For when we were still without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.
simplify: When we were powerless to help ourselves, at just the right time Christ died for people who were doing wrong. For you, this means God acted for you when you couldn't act for yourself.

text: Behold, God is my salvation, I will trust and not be afraid; "For YAH, the LORD, is my strength and song; He also has become my salvation."' Therefore with joy you will draw water From the wells of salvation.
simplify: God is the one who saves, so the speaker trusts him and refuses to be afraid. It means your strength and courage come from God, not from yourself. People will draw water from springs of salvation with joy. It means the rescue God gives is fresh and life-giving, and you can receive it gladly.

text: He sent His word and healed them, And delivered them from their destructions.
simplify: God sent his word and healed them, rescuing them from death. His word is powerful enough to restore a person's health and life.

text: Preserve me, O God, for in You I put my trust.
simplify: David asks God to keep him safe because he has placed his trust in God rather than in himself. It invites the reader to make God their refuge when they feel vulnerable.

text: Your word is a lamp to my feet And a light to my path.
simplify: God's word is light for the next step, not the whole map. That is enough to keep walking.

text: Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
simplify: If you are bringing an offering to God and remember that someone has something against you, stop. It means broken relationships matter to God even during worship. Leave your offering, go make peace with that person first, then come back and give your gift. It means settling conflict with others takes priority over religious ritual.

text: Not that I speak in regard to need, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content: I know how to be abased, and I know how to abound. Everywhere and in all things I have learned both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
simplify: Paul says he isn't talking about being in need, because he has learned to be content wherever he is. It means contentment is something you learn, not something that depends on having enough. Paul has learned how to handle both plenty and poverty, being full or hungry, having much or little. It means you can be steady in any situation, whether life is easy or hard. You can face this because he strengthens you, not because you are strong. Strength is borrowed.

text: And you, who once were alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now He has reconciled in the body of His flesh through death, to present you holy, and blameless, and above reproach in His sight-- if indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and are not moved away from the hope of the gospel which you heard, which was preached to every creature under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.
simplify: They were once estranged from God and hostile toward him because of their evil behavior, but now he has brought them back. It means their past separation has been genuinely reversed. Christ accomplished this through his physical death, so that they could stand before God holy, blameless, and free from accusation. It means their standing before God is secure because of what Christ did, not their own record. This holds true as long as they stay grounded in faith and don't drift from the hope of the good news, which has been proclaimed everywhere and which Paul serves. It means continuing in trust matters, and the message is for all people.

text: It is good to give thanks to the LORD, And to sing praises to Your name, O Most High; To declare Your lovingkindness in the morning, And Your faithfulness every night, On an instrument of ten strings, On the lute, And on the harp, With harmonious sound.
simplify: Praising God and singing to him is a good and worthwhile thing to do. It reminds us that worship is not a burden but a healthy habit for our lives. We should tell others about God's kindness in the morning and his faithfulness at night. It means making gratitude to God a regular part of every day. This verse simply describes the music used to praise God, played on stringed and quiet-sounding instruments. It shows that worship can include music of different kinds.

text: These things I have spoken to you, that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world."
simplify: Trouble is promised, and so is his victory over it. You can have peace in the middle of it.

text: This poor man cried out, and the LORD heard him, And saved him out of all his troubles.
simplify: A helpless person cried out and God heard and rescued him from every trouble. The reader can call on God even when they feel weak and overwhelmed.

text: Then you will prosper, if you take care to fulfill the statutes and judgments with which the LORD charged Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and of good courage; do not fear nor be dismayed.
simplify: David says things will go well if Solomon carefully keeps God's laws, and tells him to be strong and courageous without fear. For the reader, success is tied to faithful obedience and courage rather than to worry.

text: My voice You shall hear in the morning, O LORD; In the morning I will direct it to You, And I will look up.
simplify: David prays first thing in the morning and then waits expectantly to see what God will do. It encourages the reader to start each day with prayer and to watch for God's answer.

text: Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, But to Your name give glory, Because of Your mercy, Because of Your truth.
simplify: The writer asks that all the credit go to God, not to us, because his kindness and faithfulness are what deserve praise. It reminds us to point people toward God rather than seeking attention for ourselves.

text: Do not lie to one another, since you have put off the old man with his deeds, and have put on the new man who is renewed in knowledge according to the image of Him who created him, where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcised nor uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave nor free, but Christ is all and in all.
simplify: Stop lying to each other, since you've taken off your old self with its habits. Honesty should mark your relationships now. You've put on a new self that is being renewed in knowledge to reflect its Maker. You are being changed to become more like the God who made you. In this new life there's no difference between Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free; Christ is everything and in everyone. No one is excluded or ranked above another in him.

text: By faith Moses, when he became of age, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the passing pleasures of sin, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt; for he looked to the reward.
simplify: Moses chose not to be known as the princess's son when he grew up. Faith may mean turning down privilege for the sake of something greater. Moses chose to suffer with God's people rather than enjoy sin's short-lived pleasures. Faith sees that lasting good is worth more than quick comfort. Moses counted the shame he bore for God's sake as worth more than Egypt's riches, because he looked to his reward. Faith keeps its eyes on what God will give.

text: Then He said to them, "Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men." rm820They immediately left their nets and followed Him.
simplify: Jesus told them to follow him, and he would make them fishers of people. Following Jesus means he will use our everyday skills to help others find him.

text: But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
simplify: Paul says God is over Christ, Christ is over every man, and the man is over the woman in God's order. It means God has a structure of authority, and each person relates to him within it.

text: Now when He was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in His name when they saw the signs which He did.
simplify: Many people in Jerusalem believed in Jesus because of the miracles they saw. Seeing powerful signs can start faith, but it isn't the deepest kind of trust.

text: By faith Noah, being divinely warned of things not yet seen, moved with godly fear, prepared an ark for the saving of his household, by which he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.
simplify: Noah believed God's warning about a flood no one could see yet and built the boat that saved his family. Trusting God's word can save you and those you love, even when the world laughs.

text: Though they join forces, the wicked will not go unpunished; But the posterity of the righteous will be delivered.
simplify: Evildoers will not escape punishment, but the children of the upright will be safe. Do what is right, because God's justice is certain and he protects the families of the honest.

text: Look at the birds of the air, for they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they?
simplify: Look at the birds: they don't plant or store grain, yet your Father feeds them, and you matter far more than they do. If God cares for birds, he'll care for you.

text: I am the LORD your God, Who brought you out of the land of Egypt; Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
simplify: God reminds them he is the Lord who brought them out of Egypt and tells them to open their mouths wide so he can fill them. It shows God as a generous provider who wants his people to ask him for what they need.

text: For You are my hope, O Lord GOD; You are my trust from my youth.
simplify: He says God is the one he hopes in, and that he has trusted God since he was young. It reminds the reader that a lifelong trust in God is worth holding on to.

text: And above all things have fervent love for one another, for "love will cover a multitude of sins."
simplify: Above everything else, love each other deeply, because love covers over a great many sins. Real love forgives and does not keep a record of wrongs.

text: I will wait for You, O You his Strength; For God is my defense.
simplify: David says God is his strength and his safe place, so he will wait in hope for him. When you feel weak, you can put your hope in God as your strong defense.

text: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy.
simplify: Wisdom from God is pure, peace-loving, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good deeds, fair, and sincere. Ask God for this kind of wisdom and let it shape how you deal with others.

text: Instead of your shame you shall have double honor, And instead of confusion they shall rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land they shall possess double; Everlasting joy shall be theirs.
simplify: Because they suffered double grief and shame, they will receive double reward in their own land and enjoy lasting joy. The reader can trust that God repays past suffering with more than enough blessing.

text: "Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, And all the remnant of the house of Israel, Who have been upheld by Me from birth, Who have been carried from the womb: Even to your old age, I am He, And even to gray hairs I will carry you! I have made, and I will bear; Even I will carry, and will deliver you.
simplify: God calls his people to listen and reminds them he has carried them since the day they were born. You are not a burden he resents; he has been holding you up from the very start. God promises that even in old age he will stay the same and keep caring for the people he made. You can count on him to carry you to the end of your life, not just the beginning.

text: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.
simplify: The Spirit of truth will guide them into all truth, speaking only what he hears and telling them what is to come. It means you can trust the Holy Spirit to lead you into what is true.

text: He has shown you, O man, what is good; And what does the LORD require of you But to do justly, To love mercy, And to walk humbly with your God?
simplify: God has told you what he wants: act justly, love mercy, walk humbly. Simple to say, and harder than it sounds.

text: The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul; The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple; The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart; The commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes; The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever; The judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether.
simplify: God's teaching is perfect and refreshes your inner life, and his trustworthy word gives wisdom even to those who feel foolish. You can rely on what God says to guide you. God's commands are right and bring joy to the heart, and his clear instruction helps you see things properly. Following God's ways makes life better, not worse. Revering God is pure and lasts forever, and his judgments are true and completely fair. You can trust that God's standards are good and never go out of date.

text: But the ones that fell on the good ground are those who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, keep it and bear fruit with patience.
simplify: The seed on good soil represents people who hear God's word, hold onto it with an honest heart, and patiently produce fruit. Lasting faith means keeping God's word and letting it change us over time.

text: You have turned for me my mourning into dancing; You have put off my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness, To the end that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent. O LORD my God, I will give thanks to You forever.
simplify: God turned David's sadness into dancing and replaced his mourning clothes with joy. It shows that God can completely change a person's situation from grief to gladness. David wants to sing God's praise and never be silent, thanking him forever. It shows that when God helps us, the natural response is lasting gratitude.

text: And in that day you will say: "O LORD, I will praise You; Though You were angry with me, Your anger is turned away, and You comfort me.
simplify: The speaker thanks God because his anger has passed and he has been comforted. It means you can thank God for forgiveness and for the relief that comes after hard times.

text: In the multitude of my anxieties within me, Your comforts delight my soul.
simplify: When anxious thoughts crowd in, God's comfort brings joy to the soul. It assures the reader that God's comfort can reach even a troubled mind.

text: "For I will look on you favorably and make you fruitful, multiply you and confirm My covenant with you.
simplify: God promises to look on his people with favor, bless them with children, and keep his covenant with them. For the reader, it means God delights in his people and remains faithful to his promises.

text: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.
simplify: They all joined together constantly in prayer, along with the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers. It means unity and prayer were central to the early church, and the reader is shown a model of depending on God together.

text: But the mercy of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting On those who fear Him, And His righteousness to children's children, To such as keep His covenant, And to those who remember His commandments to do them.
simplify: God's mercy lasts forever for those who honor him, and it reaches their children and grandchildren. The reader can trust that God's faithfulness outlasts their own short life. This promise is for those who keep God's covenant and remember to obey his commands. It tells the reader that God's lasting mercy is joined with a life that follows him.

text: Those from among you Shall build the old waste places; You shall raise up the foundations of many generations; And you shall be called the Repairer of the Breach, The Restorer of Streets to Dwell In.
simplify: Your people will rebuild the old ruins and restore foundations from long ago, and you will be called the one who repairs broken walls and makes paths usable again. It means faithful, generous living leaves a lasting mark by restoring what was broken, and the reader can be part of rebuilding their community.

text: For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, so that you do not do the things that you wish.
simplify: The flesh and the Spirit are opposed to each other, so you cannot do whatever you want. For you, it means expect an inner struggle, and let the Spirit win.

text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying: "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you; Before you were born I sanctified you; I ordained you a prophet to the nations."
simplify: This line marks the start of God speaking directly to Jeremiah. It signals that what follows is a personal message from God to him. God says he knew and set apart Jeremiah before he was even born, and gave him a job as a prophet to the nations. It means God's call comes from his own choice and plan, not from our qualifications.

text: My son, hear the instruction of your father, And do not forsake the law of your mother; For they will be a graceful ornament on your head, And chains about your neck.
simplify: Listen to your father's instruction and don't reject your mother's teaching. The people who raised you often have lessons worth keeping. Good teaching from your parents is like a crown on your head and a fine necklace around your neck. It adds honor and beauty to your life when you accept it.

text: But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, surely the kingdom of God has come upon you.
simplify: If Jesus drives out demons by the Spirit of God, then God's kingdom has truly arrived among them. The healing power shows God is at work.

text: Therefore be imitators of God as dear children.
simplify: God loves you like a father loves his children, so you should want to act like him. Let that be your aim in everyday life.

text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
simplify: Jesus is the same yesterday, today and forever. The one you trusted then is the one you have now.

text: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you shall not be burned, Nor shall the flame scorch you.
simplify: The water and the fire are not removed, but you do not go through them alone. His presence is the protection.

text: Then God blessed them, and God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it; have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth."
simplify: God blessed the first humans and told them to have children, fill the earth, and rule over the animals. God gives people a purpose: to grow, to care for the world, and to manage it responsibly.

text: Jesus said to him, "If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes."
simplify: Jesus picked up on the father's 'if you can' and said everything is possible for the one who believes. He was turning the focus from his own power to the father's faith.

text: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself for her, that He might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the word, that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish.
simplify: Husbands, love your wives just as Christ loved the church and gave himself for it. Christ gave himself to make the church holy, cleansing it by the washing of water through the word. He did this to present the church to himself in splendor, without any spot or wrinkle or anything like that, but holy and without blame.

text: But You, O LORD, do not be far from Me; O My Strength, hasten to help Me!
simplify: David pleads with God, his strength, not to stay far off but to hurry and help. You can ask God to act quickly when you are in trouble.

text: For unto us a Child is born, Unto us a Son is given; And the government will be upon His shoulder. And His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
simplify: A child will be born and a son given, and he will rule with titles like Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace. This is a prophecy of Jesus, God's gift of a perfect ruler.

text: Have mercy on me, O LORD, for I am weak; O LORD, heal me, for my bones are troubled.
simplify: He begs God for mercy because his whole body feels weak and sick. Readers can see that it is okay to ask God for healing when we are worn out.

text: The LORD redeems the soul of His servants, And none of those who trust in Him shall be condemned.
simplify: God rescues those who serve him, and no one who trusts him will be put to shame. The reader can put their hope in God and be confident they will not be let down.

text: A man's heart plans his way, But the LORD directs his steps.
simplify: You can plan your path, but God is the one who actually directs your steps. Make your plans, but hold them loosely and let God lead.

text: Let the wicked forsake his way, And the unrighteous man his thoughts; Let him return to the LORD, And He will have mercy on him; And to our God, For He will abundantly pardon.
simplify: Wicked people should stop doing wrong and turn back to God, who will freely forgive them. No matter what you've done, God is ready to show mercy.

text: Those who sow in tears Shall reap in joy.
simplify: Sowing seed while crying means hard, painful work now, but it ends in a joyful harvest. Your tears and effort in hard times are not wasted.

text: He who overcomes shall inherit all things, and I will be his God and he shall be My son.
simplify: Those who stay faithful through hardship will inherit all these things and be called God's own children. For you, it means your endurance is not wasted.

text: I will praise the LORD according to His righteousness, And will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
simplify: David ends by praising God for being fair and good. It means after bringing our problems to God, we can still thank him because he is right in all he does.

text: As one whom his mother comforts, So I will comfort you; And you shall be comforted in Jerusalem."
simplify: Just as a mother comforts her child, God will comfort his people, and that comfort will be found in Jerusalem. It means God's comfort is personal and tender, like a mother's, not cold or distant.

text: "Do not fear, for you will not be ashamed; Neither be disgraced, for you will not be put to shame; For you will forget the shame of your youth, And will not remember the reproach of your widowhood anymore.
simplify: God says his people don't need to be afraid of shame or disgrace, because the humiliation of their past will be forgotten. The reader can let go of old shame and sorrow, since God promises a future without them.

text: In Him also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things according to the counsel of His will, that we who first trusted in Christ should be to the praise of His glory.
simplify: In Christ we receive an inheritance, because God marked us out beforehand and works everything according to his plan. The reader can be confident that their future is secure in God's hands. God's purpose is that we who hoped in Christ first would bring him praise. The reader's hope and life can be a way of honoring God.

text: But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven and tossed by the wind.
simplify: Ask God in faith without wavering, because a doubting person is like a wave tossed by wind. The reader should pray with steady trust rather than a divided heart.

text: You who love the LORD, hate evil! He preserves the souls of His saints; He delivers them out of the hand of the wicked.
simplify: If you love God, you will turn away from what is evil. He protects those who belong to him and rescues them from harm.

text: And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God.
simplify: Don't let the world around you shape how you think and act; instead let God change your mind from the inside out. As you do, you'll come to see for yourself what God's good and perfect will is.

text: Yet in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
simplify: In all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us. Through Christ's love, you don't just survive hardship—you overcome it.

text: As they ministered to the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, "Now separate to Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."
simplify: While the leaders were worshiping and fasting, the Holy Spirit told them to set apart Barnabas and Saul for a special mission. God sometimes makes his plans clear when people are focused on him.

text: Husbands, likewise, dwell with them with understanding, giving honor to the wife, as to the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.
simplify: Husbands must live thoughtfully with their wives, honoring them as weaker in body yet equally heirs of God's gift of life. Treating a wife badly damages your own prayer life.

text: Remember His marvelous works which He has done, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth, O seed of Abraham His servant, You children of Jacob, His chosen ones!
simplify: Remember the great things God has done, his miracles, and the judgments he has spoken. It means recalling God's past faithfulness helps us trust him now. This speaks to the descendants of Abraham and Jacob—God's chosen people. It means we should see ourselves as part of God's family and remember we belong to him.

text: We are confident, yes, well pleased rather to be absent from the body and to be present with the Lord.
