simplify: We are confident and would rather leave this body and be at home with the Lord. The reader can face death with hope, knowing that being with the Lord is better.

text: For all the promises of God in Him are Yes, and in Him Amen, to the glory of God through us.
simplify: All of God's promises find their yes in Christ, and through him we say amen to God's glory. Every promise God made is fulfilled and made certain in Jesus, so you can trust what God has said.

text: Wait on the LORD; Be of good courage, And He shall strengthen your heart; Wait, I say, on the LORD!
simplify: David tells himself and others to wait for the Lord with hope and courage. For the reader, it means trusting God often means waiting, and that waiting is where strength grows.

text: But I know that when I come to you, I shall come in the fullness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.
simplify: Paul is sure that when he comes, he will bring the full blessing of Christ. Expect God's blessing when believers meet and share in his work.

text: But I will hope continually, And will praise You yet more and more.
simplify: Even so, he says he will keep hoping and keep praising God more and more. It shows that hope and praise can continue even while trouble is still going on.

text: But above all these things put on love, which is the bond of perfection.
simplify: Above all these, put on love, which binds everything together in perfect unity. Love is what holds all the other virtues together.

text: For You have armed me with strength for the battle; You have subdued under me those who rose against me.
simplify: God arms David with strength for battle and brings his opponents down. It means God is the one who gives the ability to face and overcome opposition.

text: Therefore let us pursue the things which make for peace and the things by which one may edify another.
simplify: So let's pursue what makes for peace and what builds each other up.

text: Come, and let us return to the LORD; For He has torn, but He will heal us; He has stricken, but He will bind us up.
simplify: The people are calling each other to return to God, trusting that even though he has punished them, he is the one who will heal and restore them. It means you can turn back to God after failure, believing he repairs what sin has broken.

text: Because you have made the LORD, who is my refuge, Even the Most High, your dwelling place, No evil shall befall you, Nor shall any plague come near your dwelling; For He shall give His angels charge over you, To keep you in all your ways.
simplify: Because you have made the Lord your refuge and resting place, you are in his hands. Choosing God as your shelter is what makes this protection yours. No evil or sickness will come near your home. God's protection extends to where you live. God gives his angels charge over your path. You are watched over more than you can see.

text: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, And the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
simplify: Revering the Lord is where wisdom begins, and knowing the Holy One gives you understanding. This means real wisdom starts with taking God seriously, so let respect for God shape how you think and live.

text: Without counsel, plans go awry, But in the multitude of counselors they are established.
simplify: Plans fail without good advice, but they succeed when many wise people guide them. Ask for counsel before you commit to big decisions.

text: For His anger is but for a moment, His favor is for life; Weeping may endure for a night, But joy comes in the morning.
simplify: Hard nights are real, but they are not the end of the story. God's kindness comes back like morning.

text: "Behold, I am coming as a thief. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame."
simplify: Jesus warns that he will come unexpectedly, and those who stay faithful and ready are blessed. It encourages the reader to live watchfully and stay loyal to God.

text: And the twenty-four elders who sat before God on their thrones fell on their faces and worshiped God, saying: "We give You thanks, O Lord God Almighty, The One who is and who was and who is to come, Because You have taken Your great power and reigned.
simplify: The twenty-four elders fall on their faces before God in worship. This means heaven's leaders respond to God's victory with humble praise, not pride. They thank the Lord God Almighty, who is and was, because he has taken his great power and begun to reign. This means God's rule is something to be thankful for, not feared by his people.

text: "Comfort, yes, comfort My people!" Says your God. "Speak comfort to Jerusalem, and cry out to her, That her warfare is ended, That her iniquity is pardoned; For she has received from the LORD's hand Double for all her sins."
simplify: God tells his people to be comforted and reassured. For the reader, it means God cares about your pain and wants you to receive comfort, not just give it. God says Jerusalem's hard time of punishment is over and she has paid more than enough. For the reader, it means guilt and suffering do not last forever with God; he speaks tenderly when the hardship ends.

text: Blessed be the Lord, Who daily loads us with benefits, The God of our salvation!Selah Our God is the God of salvation; And to GOD the Lord belong escapes from death.
simplify: The writer praises God, who carries his people day after day. The reader is reminded that God's help isn't occasional but daily. God is the one who saves, and he holds the ways out of death. The reader can look to God for rescue even when things seem hopeless.

text: Let him who is taught the word share in all good things with him who teaches.
simplify: Anyone who receives teaching should share good things with the one who teaches them. It means supporting those who teach you God's word is a fitting response.

text: And they continued steadfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers.
simplify: The first believers made learning from the apostles, sharing meals, and praying a steady priority. It means we should build our lives around learning about Jesus and being with other believers, not just fitting faith in when it's convenient.

text: Do not withhold Your tender mercies from me, O LORD; Let Your lovingkindness and Your truth continually preserve me.
simplify: He asks God to keep showing mercy and faithfulness and to protect him always. It means he depends on God's steady kindness to keep him safe.

text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
simplify: The Word was with God and was God. Jesus was not an afterthought; he was there from the beginning.

text: "If you love Me, keep My commandments.
simplify: Jesus ties love for him to keeping his commands. Love here isn't just a feeling; it shows up in how you actually live.

text: For you see your calling, brethren, that not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called.
simplify: Paul points out that not many of the Corinthian believers were impressive by worldly standards of wisdom, power, or status. It reminds the reader that God often chooses ordinary people, so no one needs to feel disqualified.

text: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment, a devout man and one who feared God with all his household, who gave alms generously to the people, and prayed to God always.
simplify: A Roman army officer named Cornelius lived in Caesarea. He was an important man, but the story shows that God notices ordinary people too, whatever their rank or background. Cornelius took God seriously, prayed regularly, and gave generously to the poor, and his whole household followed his example. His life shows that sincere faith shows up in how we treat God and other people.

text: Then all the multitude kept silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul declaring how many miracles and wonders God had worked through them among the Gentiles.
simplify: The whole crowd grew quiet as Barnabas and Paul reported the signs and wonders God had done among the non-Jews. Hearing evidence of God's power silences arguments and builds faith.

text: Nor is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved."
simplify: Salvation is found in no one else, because no other name has been given by which people can be saved. Jesus is the only way to be saved, and that is true for everyone.

text: For the LORD God is a sun and shield; The LORD will give grace and glory; No good thing will He withhold From those who walk uprightly.
simplify: God is like sun and shield, giving light, protection, grace, and honor, and he withholds no good thing from those who walk rightly. It encourages the reader to trust God's generosity and care.

text: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; But we will remember the name of the LORD our God.
simplify: Some trust in chariots and horses, meaning military power, but God's people trust in the Lord. Real safety comes from God, not from human strength or weapons.

text: Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling, And to present you faultless Before the presence of His glory with exceeding joy, To God our Savior, Who alone is wise, Be glory and majesty, Dominion and power, Both now and forever. Amen.
simplify: God is able to keep you from stumbling and present you blameless before his glory with great joy. It means your security and final joy rest in God's power, not your own. To the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ, be glory, majesty, power, and authority before all time, now, and forever. It means God alone deserves all honor and praise eternally.

text: Behold, the eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him, On those who hope in His mercy, To deliver their soul from death, And to keep them alive in famine.
simplify: The Lord watches over those who honor him and put their hope in his kindness. It means God pays special attention to people who trust him and respect him. God keeps them from death and sustains them when they are in need. It means God protects and provides for those who hope in him, especially in hard times.

text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another."
simplify: Jesus gave them a new command: love one another the same way he has loved them. His kind of love, self-giving and practical, is the mark of his followers. Everyone will know you are my disciples by the love you have for each other. Love between his followers is the clearest sign of belonging to Jesus.

text: But without faith it is impossible to please Him, for he who comes to God must believe that He is, and that He is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him.
simplify: Faith pleases God, and seeking him is the point. He is not hiding from people who look.

text: Jude, a bondservant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, To those who are called, sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ: Mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.
simplify: Jude introduces himself as a servant of Jesus and brother of James, writing to people God has chosen, made holy, and kept safe for Jesus. It reminds you that you belong to God and are protected by him. Jude wishes his readers more mercy, peace, and love. It means God wants these good things to grow in your life.

text: My flesh and my heart fail; But God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
simplify: His body and heart may wear out, but God is his rock and his lasting inheritance. When everything else fails, God remains strong and forever yours.

text: We are hard-pressed on every side, yet not crushed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed-- always carrying about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our body.
simplify: Paul describes being pressed hard on every side but not crushed, and being puzzled but not left without a way forward. For the reader, it means hard times are real, but they don't have to trap or defeat you. Paul says they are hunted and knocked down but never abandoned or destroyed. For the reader, it means even when life hits hard, God has not left you on your own. Paul says his body constantly carries the dying of Jesus, so that Jesus' life can also be seen in him. For the reader, it means when you share in suffering for Jesus, his life becomes visible through you.

text: The mouth of the righteous speaks wisdom, And his tongue talks of justice.
simplify: A good person's speech is wise and speaks what is right. What comes out of your mouth shows what's in your heart.

text: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, But he who heeds counsel is wise.
simplify: A foolish person thinks their own way is always right, but a wise person listens to advice. Be willing to hear others, because you don't always see your own mistakes.

text: The hope of the righteous will be gladness, But the expectation of the wicked will perish.
simplify: Good people's hopes bring joy, but the wicked have nothing to look forward to. Put your hope in what will not disappoint.

text: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.
simplify: Everyone on earth worships the beast except those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life from the beginning. The reader is reminded that belonging to the crucified Lamb is what protects a person from deception.

text: All the angels stood around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God, saying: "Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom, Thanksgiving and honor and power and might, Be to our God forever and ever. Amen."
simplify: All the angels around the throne fall face down and worship God. Heaven's proper response to God's saving work is humble worship. The angels give God blessing, glory, wisdom, and power forever. God deserves wholehearted praise that never ends.

text: The LORD is my light and my salvation; Whom shall I fear? The LORD is the strength of my life; Of whom shall I be afraid?
simplify: If God is your light and your rescue, fear has less ground to stand on. Courage grows from who is with you.

text: Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong.
simplify: Stay alert, hold firmly to the faith, and be courageous and strong. The Christian life requires watchfulness and strength, not passive drifting.

text: Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us (for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree"), that the blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
simplify: Christ freed us from the law's curse by becoming a curse for us when He was hung on a tree. It means Jesus took the punishment we deserved so we could be free. Christ's work means the blessing promised to Abraham reaches the Gentiles, and believers receive the promised Spirit through faith. It means God's blessing and His Spirit come to everyone who believes, not just one group.

text: In my distress I called upon the LORD, And cried out to my God; He heard my voice from His temple, And my cry came before Him, even to His ears.
simplify: In his distress David cried to God, and God heard his prayer from his temple. The reader can be sure that God actually listens when they call out in trouble.

text: For the LORD loves justice, And does not forsake His saints; They are preserved forever, But the descendants of the wicked shall be cut off.
simplify: God loves justice and will not abandon those who belong to him; they are kept safe forever, while the offspring of the wicked will be cut off.

text: Of old You laid the foundation of the earth, And the heavens are the work of Your hands.
simplify: God laid the foundations of the earth and made the heavens long ago. It reminds the reader that the God they pray to is the Creator.

text: And the Lord said, "Simon, Simon! Indeed, Satan has asked for you, that he may sift you as wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith should not fail; and when you have returned to Me, strengthen your brethren."
simplify: Jesus warned Simon that Satan had asked to sift him like wheat, meaning to test him severely. Even strong believers can face intense spiritual testing. Jesus said he had prayed that Simon's faith would not fail, and told him to strengthen others once he recovered. Jesus prays for his followers, and restored failure can become a source of help for others.

text: For as we have many members in one body, but all the members do not have the same function, so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.
simplify: Just as one body has many parts and each part does a different job, so it is among believers. Though we are many people, we are joined together as one body in Christ, and each of us belongs to and needs the others.

text: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, But he who hates bribes will live.
simplify: Someone greedy for profit brings trouble on his own family, but a person who refuses bribes will live. Don't let money ruin the people closest to you.

text: And the multitudes with one accord heeded the things spoken by Philip, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did.
simplify: The crowds paid close attention to what Philip said because they saw the miracles he performed. Miracles got their attention, but the message was what mattered.

text: Then Peter said to them, "Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
simplify: Repent, be baptised, and receive the gift of the Spirit. It is an invitation with a promise inside it.

text: And the LORD, He is the One who goes before you. He will be with you, He will not leave you nor forsake you; do not fear nor be dismayed."
simplify: He leads, he stays, he does not abandon you. You can move forward even while you are still afraid.

text: But you, beloved, building yourselves up on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.
simplify: Jude tells believers to build themselves up in their holy faith and pray in the Holy Spirit. It means you grow spiritually through faith and prayer. Keep yourselves in God's love while waiting for eternal life through Jesus' mercy. It means stay close to God and live in expectation of his mercy.

text: Now He who has prepared us for this very thing is God, who also has given us the Spirit as a guarantee.
simplify: God himself prepared us for this future and gave us his Spirit as a down payment guaranteeing what is coming. The reader can trust that the Spirit inside them is God's pledge that this hope is real.

text: But let us who are of the day be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and as a helmet the hope of salvation.
simplify: Since we belong to the day, let's stay clear-headed, protected by faith, love, and the hope of being saved. These three keep you steady when pressure comes.

text: Hatred stirs up strife, But love covers all sins.
simplify: Hatred stirs up conflict, but love overlooks faults. Choosing love calms quarrels instead of fueling them.

text: Therefore we do not lose heart. Even though our outward man is perishing, yet the inward man is being renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, is working for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory, while we do not look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporary, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
simplify: Paul says they don't wear out or quit, because even though their bodies are wearing down, their inner selves are being renewed every day. For the reader, it means aging or hardship on the outside doesn't stop God from refreshing you inside. Paul says today's troubles are light and short compared to the far greater and lasting glory they are producing for us. For the reader, it means your present pain is not the end of the story and is worth far less than what's coming. Paul says to fix your eyes not on what you can see but on what you can't see, because visible things are temporary while invisible things last forever. For the reader, it means let eternal realities, not just what's in front of you, shape your focus.

text: Therefore My people shall know My name; Therefore they shall know in that day That I am He who speaks: "Behold, it is I."' How beautiful upon the mountains Are the feet of him who brings good news, Who proclaims peace, Who brings glad tidings of good things, Who proclaims salvation, Who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
simplify: God promises that his people will finally know his name and recognize that he is the one speaking to them. For the reader, it means God is not distant; he makes himself known to those who belong to him. The person who brings good news of peace and salvation is called beautiful as they come over the mountains. It means the reader should value those who announce that God is in charge, and can be one of them.

text: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, And uphold me by Your generous Spirit.
simplify: He asks for the joy of being saved to return and for a willing spirit to hold him up. It means God's salvation brings joy and strength to keep going.

text: Keep your heart with all diligence, For out of it spring the issues of life.
simplify: What you let into your heart shapes your whole life. Guard it like something valuable.

text: The LORD will guide you continually, And satisfy your soul in drought, And strengthen your bones; You shall be like a watered garden, And like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail.
simplify: God will guide you always, give you water in dry places, strengthen your bones, and make you like a well-watered garden and a spring that never runs dry. It means God sustains those who live generously, and the reader can trust God to keep them going even in hard, dry seasons.

text: But there is forgiveness with You, That You may be feared.
simplify: God chooses to forgive, and that forgiveness makes people respect and honor him. You can count on God's forgiveness rather than fear that he is only keeping score.

text: Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint; But happy is he who keeps the law.
simplify: Without guidance from God, people run wild, but whoever follows God's law is happy. It tells the reader that God's instruction brings order and blessing.

text: To him who overcomes I will grant to sit with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.
simplify: Everyone who perseveres will be given a place with Jesus on his throne, just as he overcame and sat down with his Father on his throne. It means the reader's faithful endurance leads to sharing in Jesus's victory and honor.

text: Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom which cannot be shaken, let us have grace, by which we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear.
simplify: Since we're receiving a kingdom that can never be shaken, let's be thankful and worship God in a way that pleases him, with reverence and awe.

text: Therefore comfort each other and edify one another, just as you also are doing.
simplify: Keep encouraging each other and helping each other grow, just as you've already been doing. Your words and support really do strengthen the people around you.

text: In God (I will praise His word), In the LORD (I will praise His word), In God I have put my trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
simplify: David repeats that he will praise God's word, both as God and as Lord. God's promises are worth praising because they are completely reliable. Again David says that trusting God means he will not be afraid of what people can do. Trusting God's promises is the answer to fear of people.

text: Now thanks be to God who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and through us diffuses the fragrance of His knowledge in every place.
simplify: Paul praises God, who always leads us to victory in Christ and spreads the knowledge of him everywhere through us. It means God uses ordinary believers to make himself known.

text: "But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who spitefully use you.
simplify: Jesus told his listeners to love their enemies and do good to those who hate them. This is a radically different way of treating people who hurt you. Jesus said to bless those who curse you and pray for those who mistreat you. Instead of retaliating, his followers should respond with kindness and prayer.

text: "You are the LORD God, Who chose Abram, And brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, And gave him the name Abraham; You found his heart faithful before You, And made a covenant with him To give the land of the Canaanites, The Hittites, the Amorites, The Perizzites, the Jebusites, And the Girgashites-- To give it to his descendants. You have performed Your words, For You are righteous.
simplify: The prayer recalls how God chose Abram and led him out of Ur, giving him a new name. It shows God takes the initiative in a person's life and guides them step by step. God saw that Abraham's heart was faithful and made a promise to give his descendants the land, and God kept it. It means God notices real faithfulness and keeps his promises.

text: He has put a new song in my mouth-- Praise to our God; Many will see it and fear, And will trust in the LORD.
simplify: God gave David a new song of praise, and many people saw what happened and came to trust in God. It means your rescue and gratitude can point others toward faith.

text: Watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."
simplify: Jesus told them to watch and pray so they would not fall into temptation, because the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak. Prayer is our protection in times of testing, since our own strength is not enough.

text: Therefore we also pray always for you that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfill all the good pleasure of His goodness and the work of faith with power, that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
simplify: Paul prays constantly that God will make these believers worthy of his calling and complete every good thing their faith prompts. It encourages the reader to pray for God's power to finish his good work in them. The goal is that Jesus' name is honored through them and that they share in his honor, all by God's grace. The reader is reminded that their life is meant to bring glory to Jesus.

text: Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, Than a fatted calf with hatred.
simplify: A simple meal shared with love beats a fancy dinner served with hatred. Relationships matter more than what is on the table.

text: But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves, saying, "What shall we do to these men? For, indeed, that a notable miracle has been done through them is evident to all who dwell in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
simplify: The council sent Peter and John out of the room so they could discuss the matter privately. Even powerful leaders had to stop and figure out what to do. They admitted the miracle was obvious to everyone in Jerusalem and could not be denied. When God acts, even those who oppose him cannot ignore it.

text: For You will not leave my soul in Hades, Nor will You allow Your Holy One to see corruption.
simplify: David said God would not abandon his soul to the grave or let his Holy One decay. It means God does not desert his faithful one in death, which points forward to the resurrection.

text: He who overcomes shall be clothed in white garments, and I will not blot out his name from the Book of Life; but I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.
simplify: Everyone who perseveres will be dressed in white, will never be erased from God's book of life, and will be acknowledged by Jesus before the Father and the angels. It means the reader's faithful endurance is worth everything, because Jesus himself will stand up for them in heaven.

text: He will not be afraid of evil tidings; His heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.
simplify: Such a person is not afraid when bad news comes, because their confidence rests in the Lord. It tells the reader that trusting God is what keeps fear from taking over.

text: Therefore, my beloved, as you have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling; for it is God who works in you both to will and to do for His good pleasure.
simplify: Keep obeying God whether or not anyone is watching over you, and take your salvation seriously with humble reverence. It means your faith is something you actively live out, not just something you received once. God himself is at work in you, giving you both the desire and the ability to do what pleases him. So your effort isn't solo—it's powered by God's work inside you.

text: And not only that, but we also glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces perseverance; and perseverance, character; and character, hope.
simplify: We can even be glad in our troubles, because trouble teaches us to keep waiting patiently. For you, this means hard times are not wasted; they build something good in you. Patient waiting builds proven character, and proven character builds hope. For you, this means the endurance you learn now gives you solid confidence for what's ahead.

text: Because Your lovingkindness is better than life, My lips shall praise You.
simplify: He says God's faithful love is worth more than life itself, so he will praise him. It means God's love is the most valuable thing you have, even when life is hard.

text: You therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
simplify: Paul tells Timothy to draw his strength from the grace that comes through Jesus, not from himself. For the reader, it means your strength for living the faith comes from Christ, so rely on him rather than your own resources.

text: And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
simplify: Paul assures them that God, who brings peace, will soon defeat Satan under their feet. He ends with a blessing of grace from Jesus.
